brief_summary:
Postoperative delirium and other complications are important adverse outcomes following cardiac surgery. This study will integrate perioperative clinical information with molecular measurements to investigate factors associated with these outcomes and improve early risk assessment.

Eligible patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting, cardiac valve surgery, or combined procedures will be prospectively enrolled. Data collection will include demographic characteristics, medical history, preoperative medications, laboratory findings, surgical and anesthetic characteristics, and postoperative clinical outcomes.

Blood samples will be collected before surgery and approximately 24 hours after surgery, processed according to standardized procedures, and stored for subsequent analyses. Molecular investigations will include proteomic and metabolomic profiling and targeted measurement of selected biomarkers.

POD will be assessed twice daily by trained research personnel during the first 7 postoperative days or until hospital discharge, whichever occurs first. Standardized, validated delirium assessment instruments will be used in the ICU and after transfer to the ward. Other postoperative complications and recovery outcomes will be recorded prospectively.

Analyses will examine associations between clinical characteristics, molecular profiles, and postoperative outcomes. Causal inference methods will be used, where appropriate, to explore the potential causal relevance of candidate biomarkers under explicitly stated assumptions. Interpretable prediction models will be developed using clinical variables, molecular features, or their combination. Model performance will be assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and potential clinical utility. Internal validation will be performed, and temporal or external validation will be undertaken where suitable independent data are available.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of postoperative delirium
title: Biomarkers of Postoperative Complications After Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
Bronchiolitis is a common viral infection of the small airways that affects infants, particularly during respiratory syncytial virus epidemics. Some infants mainly develop feeding difficulties, with a marked reduction in milk intake or refusal to feed, while showing no immediate signs of severe respiratory impairment. These infants often need nutritional support through a nasogastric tube, which is a small tube passed through the nose into the stomach. Under usual care, starting enteral nutrition generally requires admission to a pediatric short-stay unit or a conventional inpatient ward.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether a short period of enteral nutrition provided directly in the pediatric emergency department can reduce the total number of days spent in hospital during the 14 days following inclusion, compared with usual inpatient care. The short-term pathway is called the Short-Term Enteral Nutrition Protocol in the Pediatric Emergency Room (STENP-PER).

The study will include 448 infants treated in eight pediatric emergency departments in France. Eligible infants will be between 8 completed weeks of corrected age and 11 months and 30 days of chronological age. They must have bronchiolitis, have had respiratory symptoms for at least 72 hours, and require nutritional support because their feeding has fallen below half of the usual amount during the previous 12 hours or because they refuse to feed. Infants with signs of severe respiratory, neurological, or nutritional illness, important medical risk factors, or circumstances that would make discharge or follow-up unsafe will not be included.

This is a cluster-randomized stepped-wedge study. This means that the pediatric emergency departments, rather than individual infants, will be randomly assigned to the order in which they introduce the STENP-PER pathway. All participating departments will initially provide usual inpatient care. They will then progressively switch to the new pathway over four annual respiratory syncytial virus epidemic seasons. Each department will therefore contribute information during both a usual-care period and an intervention period.

During the usual-care period, infants will be admitted to a pediatric short-stay unit or conventional inpatient ward for enteral nutrition and clinical monitoring, according to the usual procedures of each hospital.

During the STENP-PER period, trained emergency department staff will place a nasogastric tube and provide continuous enteral nutrition for six hours while monitoring the infant's general condition, breathing, vital signs, and any adverse events. A parent will remain with the infant whenever possible. Parents will receive practical education, including information and instruction on nasal clearance. After six hours, the infant will be reassessed by the clinical team. If the infant's condition allows it, the infant will return home. If hospital monitoring or treatment is still needed, the infant will be admitted according to usual care. Participation in the study will not prevent clinicians from changing or stopping the feeding procedure when this is considered necessary for the infant's safety.

The infant's health and use of healthcare services will be followed from inclusion through Day 14. Information will be obtained from hospital records and through a telephone call with the parents around Day 14. The main outcome is the total number of days spent in hospital during this period. This includes an immediate hospital stay after the first emergency department visit and any later hospitalization or rehospitalization related to the same episode of bronchiolitis or its management.

The study will also compare the percentage of infants admitted immediately, the percentage transferred to another hospital, parents' satisfaction and experience of care, parents' understanding of advice about bronchiolitis, healthcare professionals' satisfaction, and the number and type of adverse events. The investigators will also examine how well the pathway is introduced and followed in each emergency department, how acceptable it is to families and healthcare professionals, the barriers and factors supporting its use, and whether it can be maintained and transferred to other hospitals. Interviews with parents and group discussions with healthcare professionals will provide additional information about their experience. Finally, a health-economic evaluation will compare the costs of the two care strategies over 14 days.

The study is expected to show whether providing short-term enteral nutrition in the pediatric emergency department is a safe and effective alternative to systematic hospital admission for carefully selected infants with bronchiolitis and predominant feeding difficulties.
primary_outcomes: Mean total number of hospitalization days through day 14
title: Short-Term Enteral Nutrition for Infants With Bronchiolitis in Pediatric Emergency Departments

brief_summary:
Background and Rationale:

Antacids might influence the structure/degradation and therefore the allergenicity of food proteins. This study intends to perform double-blind placebo-controlled food challenges in walnut allergic patient to determine threshold dose distribution curves and to investigate the impact of antacids (proton-pump inhibitors) on the allergy eliciting dose of walnut and the severity of the clinical manifestation in walnut allergic patients.

Objectives:

Investigation of effect of Omeprazole on the threshold dose-distribution curve and the severity of the clinical manifestation of walnut allergic patients.

Outcomes:

Primary outcome Change in the threshold dose of walnut that induces an allergic reaction after the intake of therapeutic doses of omeprazole Change in the severity of walnut allergy after the intake of therapeutic doses of omeprazole.

Study design:

Multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled; cross-over design.

Selection criteria: positive case history of immediate allergic reaction(s) to walnut and presence of specific IgE to walnut defined as a positive (≥ 3 mm wheal diameter) skin prick test and/or a serum IgE to walnut ≥ 0.35 kU/L ( ImmunoCAP).

Measurements and procedures:

Skin-prick-testing with different extracts, blood sampling for immunological testing, double-blind placebo controlled food challenge with walnut with/without previous Omeprazole.

Intervention: Omeprazol versus placebo.

Number of Participants:

Two clinical centers will participate in this study, Madrid-Spain (ES) and Zürich-Switzerland (CH). The final study population for each center will consist of 30 subjects with a challenge confirmed walnut allergy. This sample size will allow to build the probabilistic models to determine threshold dose distribution curves of walnut and calculate the ED05 and ED10.
primary_outcomes: Dose of walnut protein leading to allergic reactions in 5% (ED05)
title: The Impact of Proton-pump Inhibitors on Threshold Dose Distributions

Patients who are found to have all pulmonary veins already isolated at the time of the procedure, or who are not suitable candidates for the Marshall plan-based approach, will be included in a separate observational cohort.
primary_outcomes: Between-group difference in atrial-arrhythmia burden
title: Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Assisted Marshall-Plan Strategy in Redo Persistent Atrial Fibrillation Ablation

brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous recombinant human prourokinase (rhPro-UK) in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated more than 4.5 hours and up to 24 hours after stroke onset, selected using a noncontrast computed tomography-based artificial intelligence (CT-AI) tissue-window algorithm.

A total of 826 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intravenous rhPro-UK or matching placebo, in addition to guideline-recommended standard stroke care.

The primary outcome is the proportion of participants achieving a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-1 at 90 ± 7 days. Secondary outcomes include functional outcomes, changes in neurological deficits, early neurological improvement at 24 hours and 7 days, and tissue reperfusion at 24-48 hours. Safety outcomes include symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, parenchymal hematoma, all-cause mortality, and serious systemic bleeding.
interventions: Matching Placebo for Recombinant Human Prourokinase
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With a Modified Rankin Scale Score of 0-1 at 90 Days
title: Recombinant Human Prourokinase for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Extended Window Selected by CT-Based Artificial Intelligence

brief_summary: Heart disease is the leading cause of death for women in the United States, and many women find it hard to prioritize their own health while caring for family. This randomized control trial pilot aims to test whether linking heart-healthy habits to a woman's role as a mother or grandmother can increase physical activity and improve other heart-healthy behaviors. The study will enroll mothers and grandmothers of young children, who may join as a mother-grandmother pair or on their own. All participants will complete a baseline questionnaire (self-reported cardiovascular health including physical activity), followed by 4 weeks of wearing an activity tracker (such as a Fitbit) and a post-study period questionnaire (repeating baseline measures). After the first baseline week, participants will be randomly assigned, with pairs assigned together, to an intervention or comparison group. The intervention group will complete a short online writing activity about their caregiving role and personal values, then receive 2 weeks of daily text messages linking their health and physical activity to the health of their children and family, followed by a fourth observational week where no messaging is delivered. The comparison group will also wear the tracker for 4 weeks, but will receive 2 weeks of general daily messages (a greeting + device use reminder). The main question is whether the intervention group is more engaged in the study activities during the text message period.
primary_outcomes: Fitbit Average Daily Wear Time
title: Generations for Heart Health

brief_summary:

Thirty-five participants will apply 2 pumps of the product to their entire face twice daily (morning and night) after cleansing and toning.

Efficacy will be evaluated through subject-specific self-reported questionnaires administered at Baseline, Day 14, Day 30, Day 60, and Day 90, as well as expert skin grading and before-and-after photographs taken at Baseline, Day 30, Day 60, and Day 90. The study will also assess secondary outcomes including changes in skin brightness, smoothness, radiance, and evenness of complexion.
primary_outcomes: Change in dark spot visibility as assessed by self-reported questionnaire
Change in dark spot visibility as assessed by expert skin grading of photographs
title: A Clinical Study to Assess the Effects of a Dark Spot Corrector on Dark Spots and Overall Complexion

brief_summary:
Since 2021 Copenhagen University Hospital - Hvidovre, Denmark, has offered a 2-year, highly specialised, intensive clinical weight loss programme to patients living with severe and complex obesity, who due to somatic and/or psychiatric comorbidity are not eligible for bariatric surgery. This understudied group often lacks treatment options despite significant functional impairment and high healthcare costs. The programme is based on an intensive dietary and behavioural support provided by trained dieti-cians. It begins with an 8-week period of full TDR of 800 kcal/day. During this initial phase the patients have bimonthly consultations with the dieticians, a schedule which continues throughout the first year. At week 6-8 the patients begin the treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1-RA). Until medio 2024 patients without diabetes were treated with Liraglutide, thereafter Semaglutide has been used. After week 8 the patients transition back to a normal balanced diet, guided by the dieticians. Shorter periods of TDR can be used as a rescue-strategy in cases of weight-regain during the treat-ment period. In their second year of treatment the frequency of dietician consultations de-creases to once a month. Patients are scheduled to see a physician at the beginning of the treatment, at 4 months, at 12 months and at 21 months. At the end of the programme dieticians and physicians' advice on weight loss maintenance strategies including possibilities for cessation/reducing dose of weight loss medication but there are no clinical follow up visits.

Overall research question What is the durability and long-term health effects of a hospital-based IWL-treatment programme, with specific attention to cardiometabolic health, body-composition and health-related quality of life, at least 1 year after cessation of treatment in a clinical cohort of patients living with severe obesity and multimorbidity?

Study design This study is a post-intervention observational follow-up (FU) study, evaluating the durability of the IWL-treatment offered to patients at Hvidovre Hospital since 2022. This study is a substudy under the study-compilation SHAPe, consisting of a quality-assurance project evaluating the treatment programme, this post-intervention observational FU-study, a qualitative study exploring psychosocial and socio-economic precarity mediate adherence to the programme and durability of health outcomes and a societal and economic impact study to evaluate the impact on total health care costs and labour market attachment.

The FU-visit will consist of a single investigation day at Hvidovre Hospital and will be scheduled at least 12 months after completing the treatment programme. Participants will provide blood and urine samples, undergo anthropometric measurements (weight, height, waist circumference), blood pressure assessment, and body composition analysis. They will also complete the SF-36 questionnaire and a . Additionally, they will be asked for consent to link their data to national registries for a 10-year follow-up on hospital admissions, medication use, and employment status. Biological samples may be stored for future analysis of metabolic biomarkers related to weight regulation.

Due to the clinical nature of the study, it is exploratory and descriptive and hence does not include hypothesis testing, but instead an overall research question. Thus, it is designed with a non-hierarchical outcome structure, though with certain patient-centred "key outcomes." These outcomes have been chosen to reflect what is important for patients lives with skeletal muscle mass, health-related quality of life and weight as key outcomes. Additionally, we will explore the following outcomes: fat-mass, waist circumference, use of weight-loss medication, lower body strength, blood-pressure, HbA1c, lipid levels and potential proteomic biomarkes associated with regain vs weight maintenance. We aim to include 200 participants in the FU study.
conditions: Weight Management in Adult Patients With Obesity or Overweight
primary_outcomes: Weight change
Proteomics and metabolomics related to weight-loss and weight-gain.
Change in skeletal muscle mass
Health related quality of life
title: Sustaining Health After an Intensive Weight-loss Pro-gramme

brief_summary:
Introduction:

Major abdominal surgery encompasses a broad range of surgical procedures in heterogeneous patient populations.Management of postoperative pain has received keen attention in recent years with considerable concurrent advancement in the field.Despite this improvement,postoperative pain continues to be a challenge since suboptimal postoperative pain control is a risk factor for persistent surgical pain,increased morbidity,poorer functional recovery and reduced quality of life.Therefore,analgesic strategies should regard patients' factors as well as surgical procedures peculiarities.Since efforts are made throughout the years and are of utmost importance as numerous analgesic options exist for the effective pain control after abdominal surgeries including multiple classes of drugs and routes of administration(i.e.parenteral,regional,neuraxia.)In the context of the current surgical environment where improvement has been made,emphasis is placed on precision,minimizing trauma and improving the outcome.The choice of postoperative pain analgesic modality,is at the discretion of the primary anaesthesiologist and the choice depends upon the plan favored by him/her as well as the availability of drugs and equipment.Continuous re-evaluation of analgesic strategies is a necessary step toward establishing a better pain management plan in major abdominal surgeries and to design guidelines to improve our clinical approach.

Study Objective:

The target of the study is to compare the outcome of the selected analgesic combination of local anaesthetic and opioid(ropivacaine+fentanyl or ropivacaine +morphine)for postoperative continuous infusion,aiming to relief successfully the pain,on patients undergoing major abdominal surgeries based on hemodynamic and clinical findings.

The study aims to highlight the positive impact of the chosen analgesic combination during the intraoperative period,the postoperative recovery period and also during the follow up periods in terms of physical function,pain intensity during activity,adverse effects and self efficacy.

Methods:

The study is prospective,comparative aiming to identify the pain management agents that will provide the best postoperative relief in order to be established and used as a primary choice to patients undergoing major open abdominal surgeries .All patients included will receive the same analgesic technique(epidural)chosen preoperatively by the anaesthesiologist in charge.All study participants are informed in detail and written informed consent is obtained.The study is in accordance with the regulations of the Declaration of Helsinki on human studies and the Greek legislation.

We will study 58 patients,equally divided into two groups, aged 18-80 years,administered to Evangelismos General hospital,Athens-Greece, for elective open abdominal surgeries.

In group A(p:29),we will administer for postoperative pain relief - Ropivacaine 200 ml/400 mg + Fentanyl for continuous epidural infusion for the first 5 days.The infusion will start 2 hours before the end of the operation and before the admission to the intensive care unit.

In group B(p:29),we will administer for postoperative pain relief Ropivacaine 200ml/400mg + Morphine for continuous epidural infusion for the first 5 days.The infusion will start 2 hours before the end of the operation and before the admission to the intensive care unit.
lead_sponsor: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
primary_outcomes: Pain Relief
title: Implementation of a Pain Management Plan in Major Open Abdominal Surgeries.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the drug combination Elranatamab plus Mezigdomide plus Dexametahsone works to cure patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do participants receiving Elranatamab plus Mezigdomide plus Dexametahsone achieve optimal treatment response by showing negative minimal residual disease at the end of treatment?

By evaluating the incidence of adverse events and severe adverse events, is this drug combination tolerable for participants?

All participants will receive 1 cycle of Elranatamab plus Dexamethasone followed by 5 cycles of Elranatamab plus Mezigdomide plus Dexamethasone, and 6 cycles of Elranatamab plus Mezigdomide. At this timepoint (end of cycle 12), the level of minimal residual disease will be assessed to decide if patients receive Mezigdomide alone as maintenance (for patients with negative minimal residual disease), or continue reciving Elranatamab plus Mezigdomide.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients achieving minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity.
title: Elranatamab With Mezigdomide and Dexamethasone in Patients With Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary: Bulkamid filler is a gel that we use very regularly to treat female urinary leakage during exercise. Colorectal cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in France, with close to 50,000 new cases each year. About half of the patients develop liver, lung and/or peritoneal metastases during the course of the disease.Peritoneal involvement, which accounts for approximately 8,000 new cases per year, carries the poorest prognosis, notably because of its chemoresistance.For patients with resectable colorectal peritoneal metastases,recommended optimal management combines systemic chemotherapy with complete cytoreductive surgery(CRS)in an expert center.Hyperthermic IntraPeritoneal Chemotherapy(HIPEC)may be added to CRS to eradicate residual microscopic disease and potentially improve survival.Clinical evidence on HIPEC for colorectal peritoneal carcinomatosis is heterogeneous and dominated by a randomized trial reporting no survival benefit and increased morbidity, results attributed to the oxaliplatin-based HIPEC regimen used. A separate body of evidence suggests a benefit of mitomycin-C-based HIPEC, with manageable morbidity and preserved quality of life. National and international guidelines therefore allow mitomycin-C HIPEC, but the procedure remains controversial: according to French hospital discharge data, about half of the patients treated for colorectal peritoneal carcinomatosis receive CRS plus HIPEC and the other half CRS alone.HIPEC also raises funding and efficiency issues. No specific French diagnosis-related tariff (GHS)exists for CRS plus HIPEC, whereas the procedure is costly in terms of operating time,human and material resources, and is associated with prolonged hospital stays and complications. To date, no prospective comparative data on the efficiency of CRS plus HIPEC are available in France.ECO-CHIP is a national,multicenter, prospective, comparative,non-randomized, open, non-interventional study using a " here-elsewhere " design (French RIPH category 3). Each participating center follows its own routine practice: centers performing HIPEC treat included patients with CRS plus mitomycin-C HIPEC (innovative strategy), while centers not performing HIPEC treat included patients with CRS alone (reference strategy).No change in management, examination or procedure is imposed by the protocol.the only procedure added because of the research is the completion of self-administered questionnaires (EQ-5D-5L, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-CR29 and PERI-PROM) at inclusion and at months 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24 and 36 after cytoreductive surgery. The primary objective is to assess, from the French health care system perspective and over a 36-month horizon, the efficiency (cost-utility) of cytoreductive surgery combined with mitomycin-C HIPEC versus cytoreductive surgery alone. Costs are derived from micro-costing of the index hospital stay and from individual linkage with the French National Health Data System(SNDS); utilities are derived from the EQ-5D-5L using the French value set. Secondary objectives compare the two strategies in terms of disease-free survival, peritoneal recurrence-free survival, overall survival, toxicity, postoperative complications, recurrence patterns, access to iterative complete cytoreduction, costs, budget impact for the French statutory health insurance, cost-effectiveness at 3 and 5 years, and health-related quality of life.

Study hypothesis: the addition of mitomycin-C HIPEC to complete cytoreductive surgery is an efficient strategy for the French health care system, improving disease-free survival (expected 3-year disease-free survival of 26% with CRS plus HIPEC versus 13% with CRS alone, hazard ratio 0.66) and quality-adjusted survival at an acceptable incremental cost per QALY gained.

The amount of radioactivity is small and carefully limited. After the dose, researchers will collect samples such as blood, urine and stool. These will show how much of the medicine is recovered and what it turns into in the body.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this observational study is to learn how stomach cancer that has spread to nearby lymph nodes responds to standard chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy given before surgery. In people with locally advanced gastric cancer, this pre-surgery treatment can shrink the tumor and clear cancer cells from some lymph nodes. However, it is not clear which groups of lymph nodes around the stomach still contain cancer cells after treatment. The study will also examine whether dense scarring (fibrosis) around the tumor is linked to a lower chance of cancer remaining in the lymph nodes. This information may help doctors in the future decide whether some lymph node groups can be safely left in place during surgery for people with severe scarring.

Participants in this study will receive standard pre-surgery treatment with SOX chemotherapy (S-1 plus oxaliplatin) and a PD-1 inhibitor for at least 2 cycles. After treatment, they will undergo standard gastrectomy with D2 lymph node dissection, which is the routine surgical removal of the main lymph node groups around the stomach. During surgery, the surgeon will record the degree of scarring and difficulty in separating the tissues. Lymph nodes will be collected and labeled by station so that each group can be examined separately. The study will then describe how often cancer is found in each lymph node station after treatment and explore whether scarring is related to cancer remaining in the nodes. The study will also track surgical outcomes and follow participants for up to 3 years to assess cancer recurrence and survival.

Approximately 103 participants will be enrolled. The study is expected to run from January 2027 through December 2029. Each participant will be followed for about 3 years after surgery, with clinic visits every 3 months for the first 2 years and every 6 months in the third year. This study does not assign participants to different treatments; all participants receive standard care, and the study only observes and records the results.
interventions: Neoadjuvant SOX chemotherapy combined with PD-1 inhibitor
primary_outcomes: Station-specific lymph node metastasis positivity rate after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy

Researchers will compare retinal images from patients with RPE65- or RPGR-associated IRDs with images from healthy participants, including people with and without myopia, to assess how accurately the algorithms can distinguish between these groups and monitor disease-related changes.

brief_summary:
Millions of people are hospitalized every year in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) with severe health conditions due to various causes and categories of diseases, such as stroke, Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBI), polytrauma, sepsis, and others. In recent years, there has been a remarkable increase in survival rates among patients from all diagnostic categories admitted to the ICU. However, the stay of critically ill patients in the ICU is associated with a significant reduction in physical activity, even in cases where patients can participate in an active, voluntary rehabilitation program. This prolonged immobility has been linked to the development of Intensive Care Unit-Acquired Weakness (ICU-AW) and a decline in health-related quality of life (HRQOL).

During the performance of Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), eye-hand coordination plays a crucial role. It depends on the integration of multiple brain systems and is therefore often impaired in many pathological conditions. Moreover, in recent years, the use of exercises that simulate functional tasks and activities of daily living, has been continuously increasing in physiotherapy and occupational therapy programs. Additionally, the implementation of purposeful, repetitive activity in patients with central nervous system lesions (e.g., stroke, traumatic brain injury) can lead to significant neuroplastic changes in the brain that may help improve upper limb function.

Nowadays, Virtual Reality (VR) applications are increasingly used in patient rehabilitation.

However, the application of fully immersive virtual reality devices for purposeful activities aiming to improve upper limb function in critically ill patients is an innovative intervention that has not yet been sufficiently studied to inform the development of Clinical Guidelines. Furthermore, despite its clinical significance, eye-hand coordination is not routinely assessed , and there is a limited amount of data regarding its rehabilitation, especially through VR technology.

The aim of this study, therefore, is to investigate the effect of fully immersive virtual reality on the rehabilitation of sensorimotor perception and visuomotor coordination skills, as well as on the improvement of upper limb function in critically ill patients.

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if three Ukrainian-made windlass tourniquets (SICH, DNIPRO GEN 2 and PULS) stop arterial blood flow in the arm or leg as well as the Combat Application Tourniquet (CAT Gen 7) does. The trial is in healthy adult volunteers, men and women aged 18 to 55 years. Limb tourniquets are used to stop life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg. The results will support a national standard for windlass tourniquets in Ukraine.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Does each Ukrainian tourniquet completely stop arterial blood flow below the tourniquet within 120 seconds as often as CAT Gen 7? Stopped blood flow will be confirmed by Doppler ultrasound.

Investigators will compare each Ukrainian tourniquet with CAT Gen 7 in the same participant, using one device on the arm and the other on the leg. They will look at whether blood flow is completely stopped and how quickly. They will also compare:

* pain and comfort during and after use;
* how fast normal blood flow returns after the tourniquet is removed;
* how reliably each device can be applied;
* any device problems and side effects.

Participants will:

Attend a screening visit with a medical history, physical examination, vital signs, ECG, tests for hepatitis B (HBsAg) and hepatitis C (anti-HCV) on the blood sample, and a rapid HIV test using a mouth swabblood, urine tests including pregnancy test (only for women).

Be randomly assigned to one pair of devices: CAT Gen 7 with SICH, CAT Gen 7 with DNIPRO GEN 2, or CAT Gen 7 with PULS. The order in which the two devices are used will also be chosen at random.

Have a tourniquet applied by trained study staff on two visits at least 24 hours apart. Each time, a different device is used on a different limb (upper arm or thigh), for no longer than 120 seconds.

Have blood flow checked with Doppler ultrasound by a doctor who does not know which device is being used.

Have skin temperature measured, and rate their pain and comfort. Receive follow-up phone calls about 24 hours and 72 hours after the second application. A clinic visit is arranged only if a side effect is reported.

brief_summary:
Finding effective ways to slow down or prevent the development of cancer in people with Fanconi anemia (FA) is a critical medical priority. Individuals with FA are at dramatically higher risk of developing aggressive cancers, particularly of the head and neck, and these cancers are difficult to treat with standard therapies such as surgery, chemotherapy or radiation. Because options for treatment are limited and outcomes are often poor, prevention strategies are urgently needed.

In this study, the investigators will test two widely available drugs, metformin and naproxen, to evaluate whether they can lower the risk of cancer in FA patients. Metformin is commonly prescribed for type 2 diabetes, while naproxen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) frequently used for pain and inflammation. Both have shown potential in previous research to influence biological pathways linked to cancer development. By repurposing these well-known drugs, this trial aims to explore a safe, practical approach to cancer prevention in this vulnerable population.

The study, conducted at the Rockefeller University and the University of Minnesota, has several goals. First, the investigators will carefully assess the safety and tolerability of metformin and naproxen when used in participants with FA. Because these individuals can be more susceptible to metabolic disorders like diabetes compared to the general population, and may have genitourinary abnormalities related to their underlying condition, monitoring for side effects and adverse events is especially important. Second, investigators will evaluate whether intervention affects visible or microscopic changes in the mouth, where cancers often arise. This will involve performing small biopsies of oral tissue to look for cancerous or pre-cancerous lesions. Third, investigators will investigate early molecular changes using an exploratory less invasive technique: collecting cells with a soft brush, similar to a toothbrush. These samples will allow the investigators to analyze biomarkers-biological signals that can indicate increased or reduced cancer risk-before and after intervention.

Together, these approaches will provide information on whether metformin or naproxen are safe and well-tolerated in the FA population. As an additional outcome, by combining direct tissue analysis with biomarker studies, the investigators aim to detect subtle changes that precede cancer, giving us an early indication of whether the drugs are working as preventive agents.

Although this is an early-phase study, its potential significance is considerable. Demonstrating that well-tolerated, inexpensive, and widely accessible drugs may have potential to reduce cancer risk would represent a major advance for FA patients, who currently face limited options for prevention and treatment. This work may also offer insights relevant to broader cancer prevention efforts in other high-risk groups. Ultimately, our study seeks to take an important step toward changing the outlook for people with Fanconi anemia by moving the focus from late-stage treatment toward early prevention.
conditions: Squamous Cell Cancer of Head and Neck (SCCHN)

Tolerability of Intervention Regimen
title: Safety and Tolerability of Metformin and Naproxen for Cancer Prevention in Fanconi Anemia

brief_summary:
Treatment interruption in HIV care is one of the most enduring challenges to HIV programs globally and is associated with high rates of detectable virus in the blood and overall morbidity and mortality. Existing approaches to reengaging people living with HIV (PLH) have largely focused on return-to-care strategies but have not adequately addressed long-term retention after return. Effective strategies must integrate interventions that not only facilitate the return to care but also sustain engagement to prevent future lapses. Active follow-up of clients is a strategy that can promote both timely return to care and sustained long-term engagement.

The Bwelela Easy study seeks to identify person centered strategies using combinations of navigation and community-based medication delivery to both facilitate return to HIV care as well as sustain long-term reengagement post-return among individuals with treatment lapses in Zambia. The study is designed to randomly assign participants to different approaches at two different points, with the second assignment based on their earlier response. This is to compare different step-by-step combinations of approaches for improving return to care and staying in care after treatment interruptions for people living with HIV.

In the first stage (return) we will randomly assign individuals who are more than 30 days late for an appointment to routine phone outreach alone (control) versus Navigator+ Community Based medication groups. Among those who return to care, we will then re-randomly assign them in the second-stage (return and stay in care) to routine care and counseling (control), Navigator only, Navigator+ Community Based medication groups. This study advances a high priority research agenda to identify the most effective and efficient strategies for improving reengagement in care and will help maximize not only the public health impact of HIV programs but also advance strategies to improve care delivery for chronic diseases worldwide.

The data collected in this research study will be used to analyze whether the HARBOR Device is safe and effective in treating brain aneurysms.

brief_summary:
Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) has created a 'paradigm shift' within cardiac electrophysiology and the initial experience demonstrates that PFA is safe, rapid and effective compared to both radiofrequency ablation and cryoablation in atrial fibrillation (AF). Presently, AF ablation procedures in the UK using PFA are routinely performed using general anaesthetic (GA) support requiring an anaesthetist and ODP being present in all procedures. This need significantly limits the ability to use PFA technology to perform AF ablations, particularly in centres that have limited availability of GA provision.

The need for GA also leads to extended patient recovery time post procedure which impacts patient throughput and has the potential to reduce hospital bed availability. The need for GA and the potential to limit patient throughput has negative implications for all hospitals in terms of cost. PFA procedures performed elsewhere in Europe use deep sedation with IV propofol led by the ablating physician, but this is not permitted in the UK and still requires the presence of an anaesthetist.

The investigators will aim to evaluate if AF ablation using PFA is feasible during spontaneous respiration without the use of propofol. The investigators will conduct a non-randomized study comparing AF ablation using PFA vs cryoballoon under deep sedation - aiming to demonstrate that \>75% of patients can complete the PFA protocol under deep sedation without conversion to cryoballoon (due to patient intolerance). The principal aim of the study is therefore not to demonstrate superiority or comparative efficacy of one ablation modality over another but rather the ability and feasibility to deliver pulsed field ablation under deep sedation. The use of cryoablation serves as a benchmark comparator to contextualise procedural and sedation-related observations.
interventions: Deep sedation with midazolam and fentanyl or midazolam and remifentanil
primary_outcomes: Percentage of patients able to complete protocol with pulsed field ablation without conversion to cryoablaton
title: A Comparison of Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) vs Cryoablation for Atrial Fibrillation Under Deep Sedation

brief_summary:
Spinal cord injury can cause lasting difficulties with movement, sensation, bladder and bowel function, and daily activities. Epidural spinal cord stimulation delivers electrical pulses through implanted electrodes and may be used together with rehabilitation to support recovery.

This retrospective case series will review clinical records from six patients with spinal cord injury who previously received implanted epidural spinal cord stimulation at Haikou People's Hospital. Three of the patients are children. The study aims to describe changes in movement, sensation, standing and walking ability, daily activities, and other functions, as documented in the available records. It will also summarize complications related to implantation, the stimulation system, and stimulation during follow-up.

The research involves reviewing existing treatment and follow-up information. Participation in this retrospective study does not require a new implantation procedure or changes to the patient's treatment.

brief_summary:
Influenza can cause serious illness in older adults, particularly those with diabetes. Although influenza vaccination is an important preventive measure, vaccination uptake among older adults in China remains low.

This study aimed to evaluate whether different ways of presenting influenza vaccination information could encourage vaccination among older adults with diabetes in Yangzhou, China.

Adults aged 60 to 75 years with diabetes were assigned to one of four study groups: a control group without intervention text messages, a standard information group, a gain-framed information group emphasizing the benefits of vaccination, and a loss-framed information group emphasizing the potential negative consequences of not being vaccinated.

The primary outcome was influenza vaccination uptake during follow-up. Secondary outcomes included willingness to receive influenza vaccination and vaccine literacy. The study examined whether information-based interventions could improve vaccination-related outcomes compared with the control group.
primary_outcomes: Influenza Vaccination Uptake
title: Information-Based Interventions for Influenza Vaccination Among Older Adults With Diabetes in Yangzhou, China

Studies in the literature report that due to the structure of the root canals, mechanical instrumentation alone could not perform a satisfying cleaning in the canal. some areas have remained unreached and infected, thus irrigation has played a key role in the achievement of root canal treatments.

brief_summary: This study is a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial. It aims to evaluate whether an early monitoring and warning system based on a smartphone mini-program can effectively reduce the incidence of overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) and the risk of related readmission or death in cirrhotic patients within 1 month after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement. Patients with decompensated cirrhosis are at high risk of developing hepatic encephalopathy after TIPS. The traditional follow-up model often fails to capture subtle fluctuations in early neuropsychiatric symptoms during the home care period. This study plans to recruit 394 patients undergoing elective TIPS. These patients will be randomly assigned to either the mini-program intervention group or the conventional follow-up group in a 1:1 ratio. In addition to standard treatment, the intervention group will undergo daily cognitive function testing and symptom self-assessment using a dedicated mini-program for 1 month after discharge. When the system detects abnormal cognitive indicators or symptom deterioration and triggers an alert, the medical team will respond rapidly and initiate standardized interventions. The conventional follow-up group will receive standard discharge instructions and weekly telephone follow-ups. This study aims to establish a closed-loop digital management model of "home self-monitoring - intelligent early warning - medical intervention" to achieve early identification and timely intervention for covert hepatic encephalopathy, thereby tangibly improving the clinical prognosis of patients after TIPS.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital of Nanjing University Medical School
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Incidence of the Primary Composite Endpoint
title: Effect of Mini-Program Monitoring on Hepatic Encephalopathy in Post-TIPS Patients

brief_summary: Huntington's disease (HD) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder in which accelerated loss of muscle mass, strength and autonomy (physical frailty and sarcopenia) contributes to functional decline. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, four-arm parallel trial will include adults with HD and physical frailty/sarcopenia. All participants will follow a 12-week individualized, home-based multicomponent exercise program (VIVIFRAIL-based, with weekly remote monitoring) and will be randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo, creatine (CRE), beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) or combined CRE+HMB. The study will test whether combined CRE+HMB produces synergistic improvements in functional capacity, neuromuscular performance, body composition, cognition and quality of life, and will use multi-omic profiling (circulating and extracellular-vesicle microRNAs, plasma proteomics and genetics) to identify mechanisms and predictive signatures of response. Durability of effects will be assessed 6 months after the end of the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Total Functional Capacity (TFC)
title: Creatine and Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methylbutyrate (HMB) Supplementation Plus Home-Based Exercise for Sarcopenia in Huntington's Disease

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect of digital lactation nursing support on breastfeeding achievement and maternal-infant outcomes among first-time mothers.
primary_outcomes: Knowledge of primigravida women about breast feeding
title: Empowering First-Time Mothers

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a single knee injection of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) combined with hyaluronic acid (HA) works better than PRP alone or HA alone to relieve pain and improve function in physically active adults (athletes) with knee osteoarthritis. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does PRP combined with HA improve the WOMAC total score at 12 months more than PRP alone?
* How do PRP plus HA, PRP alone and HA alone compare regarding pain, function, sports activity, global improvement, satisfaction, use of rescue medication and adverse events over 24 months?

Researchers will compare three groups: PRP plus HA, PRP alone and HA alone. The PRP will be leukocyte-poor, prepared fresh, standardized to at least 1,000,000 platelets per microliter and a total dose of at least 5 billion platelets, and fully characterized according to the MIBO checklist and the AAOS/NIH minimum reporting standards.

Participants will:

* Have a blood sample collected (all groups, so that participants do not know which treatment they receive)
* Receive one ultrasound-guided injection in the target knee
* Answer questionnaires (WOMAC, KOOS, IKDC, Lysholm, Tegner and pain scale) at baseline and at 3, 6, 12 and 24 months
* Report any pain medication used, other treatments and side effects during follow-up
lead_sponsor: University of Sao Paulo General Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in WOMAC Total Score From Baseline to 12 Months
title: Platelet-Rich Plasma, Hyaluronic Acid, or Their Combination for Knee Osteoarthritis in Athletes

The aim of this study is to compare the upper extremity functional exercise capacity, upper extremity functionality, peripheral muscle strength, and quality of life of individuals with chronic non-specific neck pain with those of healthy individuals.
primary_outcomes: Upper extremity functional exercise capasity

brief_summary: This multicenter prospective observational cohort study will enroll 224 adults with a tracheostomy tube in place for at least 14 days. Within 1 week after enrollment, each participant will undergo a standardized three-station bronchoscopy through the tracheostomy tube and transnasally, with temporary tube occlusion and immediate tube replacement when required. The study will describe the prevalence, anatomic distribution, and severity of laryngotracheal lesions, including mucosal ulceration, scar formation, granulation tissue, vocal cord paralysis, subglottic stenosis, and tracheomalacia. The study will also evaluate clinical and tracheostomy-related factors associated with these lesions. No treatment is assigned by the study; the bronchoscopy is a standardized diagnostic assessment performed for research evaluation.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Any Laryngotracheal Lesion
title: Laryngotracheal Lesions in Adults With Long-Term Tracheostomy

brief_summary:
Heart disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. The Omega-3 Index (O3I) is a blood test that measures the amount of the omega-3 fats EPA and DHA in red blood cells. Research suggests that people with an O3I above 8% have a lower risk of dying from coronary heart disease than people with an O3I below 4%.

Eating fatty fish two or more times per week may help improve omega-3 status, but many people do not eat enough fish because of taste preferences or concerns about contaminants. Omega-3 supplements, such as fish oil and algae oil, can provide EPA and DHA directly and may help raise the Omega-3 Index. Research suggests that algae oil can be as effective as fish oil for increasing EPA and DHA levels.

This study will evaluate whether different fish-oil and algae-oil products-including softgels, liquids, and gummies-improve omega-3 status in healthy adults who eat little fatty fish. Participants will be asked to keep their usual diet, activity, medications, supplements, and lifestyle habits as consistent as possible during the study.
primary_outcomes: Omega-3 Index
title: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo Controlled, Parallel Virtual Clinical Trial to Investigate the Efficacy of Marine Oil Products on Omega-3 Status in Healthy Adults

brief_summary:
Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare disease in which wart-like growths caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) types 6 or 11 form in the airway. These growths can affect the voice and breathing and often come back after they are removed, meaning many children will need repeated surgeries to keep their airway open. There is no medicine approved to treat RRP in children.

This study is testing zopapogene imadenovec, an investigational immunotherapy designed to help the immune system recognize and control cells infected with HPV 6 and 11. Zopapogene imadenovec is approved in the United States for the treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.

All participants in this study will receive zopapogene imadenovec; there is no placebo group. The study drug is given as four injections under the skin over about three months. Before the first injection, participants have a standard surgical procedure to remove visible growths. Participants are then followed for at least 12 months to see how many need further surgery, and are contacted periodically for up to five years after their last injection.

The study will enroll children in two age groups, starting with older children and opening to younger children only after safety has been reviewed.
primary_outcomes: Complete response rate
title: Zopapogene Imadenovec for the Treatment of Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis in Children

brief_summary:
Cesarean delivery is one of the most frequently performed major surgical procedures worldwide. The postcesarean period is characterized by moderate to severe pain, which may adversely affect postoperative recovery, patient satisfaction, breastfeeding success, and maternal-infant bonding.

Current guidelines recommend a multimodal approach to postcesarean analgesia that reduces opioid consumption and minimizes adverse effects. The Procedure-Specific Postoperative Pain Management working group recommends multimodal protocols for elective cesarean delivery that combine systemic analgesics (regular paracetamol and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, neuraxial intrathecal morphine, and/or abdominal wall blocks, such as transversus abdominis plane and quadratus lumborum blocks.
primary_outcomes: quality of recovery-10
title: Effect of Sacral Erector Spinae Plane Block on Quality of Recovery After Cesarean Delivery: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study is looking at whether taking a nutritional supplement before and after knee replacement surgery affects normal recovery. The supplement is Xcelerated Recovery (XR), an over-the-counter supplement made with essential amino acids (EAAs), which are building blocks of protein that the body cannot make on its own.

Participants aged 65 and older with planned knee replacement surgery, and signs of nutritional risk or reduced muscle strength on short screening questionnaires, will be invited to join. Participants are assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group receives usual care plus the XR supplement, taken twice a day starting 7 days before surgery and continuing for 14 days after surgery. The other group receives usual care without the supplement. Everyone in the study wears a small temporary skin sensor (similar to a temporary tattoo) on the knee and uses a smartphone app to take scans that measure knee size. Participants also have in-person visits before surgery and 2 weeks and 1 month after surgery.

The main goal is to measure how knee and leg size (circumference) changes after surgery in each group. Researchers will also look at muscle strength, knee movement, walking and mobility tests, and reported pain. This study is not testing the supplement as a treatment for any disease or medical condition. The results may help researchers better understand how nutrition relates to normal recovery after knee replacement surgery.
primary_outcomes: Change in Mid-Patellar Circumference From Baseline
title: Nutrition and Swelling

brief_summary:
Tumor thrombus in the inferior vena cava can invade the vessel wall. Doctors must know the invasion status before surgery. The status changes the surgical plan. Preoperative imaging has limited accuracy for wall invasion. Habitat imaging divides a tumor into subregions. Each subregion is a habitat. The method uses voxel-level image features.

This study will test whether habitat imaging can diagnose inferior vena cava wall invasion. The participants have renal cell carcinoma with renal vein or inferior vena cava tumor thrombus. The study will use existing preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images. The reference standard is the pathology report from surgery.

The primary measurement is the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of the habitat model for wall invasion. The study will also measure sensitivity, specificity, calibration, and clinical utility. In an exploratory analysis, the study will compare imaging habitats with spatial transcriptomic regions. The study will use available Visium data from two participants.

This is a retrospective observational study. The study has no intervention. The study will not change clinical care. The results will show whether habitat imaging can support preoperative planning.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Performance (AUROC) of Preoperative CT/MRI Habitat Imaging for Inferior Vena Cava Wall Invasion
title: Habitat Analysis of Tumor Thrombus for Vena Cava Wall Invasion in Renal Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary:
Study Title: Randomized Controlled Clinical Study on Acupuncture Combined with Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation for Constipation-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Anxiety State.

This single-center, randomized, single-blinded sham-controlled trial enrolls adults aged 18-70 with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) and anxiety. All participants receive standardized weekly acupuncture for 4 weeks. Participants are randomly assigned 1:1 to either real daily home Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation(TEAS)at Zusanli acupoint or sham non-acupoint TEAS. The total study period lasts approximately 10 weeks, including 2-week screening, 4-week intervention and 4-week post-treatment follow-up.

The primary outcome is weekly complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBM) at week 4. Secondary outcomes cover anxiety, sleep quality, abdominal symptoms, quality of life and safety. Researchers will test whether adding real home-based TEAS to acupuncture improves bowel and emotional symptoms, and evaluate treatment safety and tolerability.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University
primary_outcomes: Weekly complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBM)
title: Acupuncture Combined With Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation for Constipation-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Anxiety State

brief_summary:
The goal of this two-arm clinical trial is to compare additional surgery with active surveillance in patients with high-risk pT1 colorectal cancer after local excision. The main questions it aims to answer are Does additional surgery result in lower rates of distant or extraluminal recurrence compared with active surveillance? How do the two treatment strategies differ in survival, complications, quality of life, and treatment-related costs?

Participants will be randomly assigned to either additional surgery or active surveillance.

Patients assigned to the surgery group will undergo standard preoperative assessment followed by additional surgery. Following surgery, patients will undergo surveillance according to the predefined follow-up protocol.

Patients assigned to the active surveillance group will not receive any additional treatment. They will undergo surveillance according to a more intensive predefined follow-up protocol.
primary_outcomes: Distant or extraluminal recurrence rate
title: T1 Colorectal Cancer After Local Excision: Decision Between Surgery and Active Surveillance (T1LDA Trial)

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether it is practical (feasible) to use a new type of imaging scan called 68Ga-FAPI PET/MRI (positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging) to evaluate how well breast cancer responds to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

brief_summary:
In Study 3, all tasks and models from Aim 1 will be evaluated in a large community sample of online participants recruited through Prolific.

Aim 3 will establish 1) requirements for testing computational algorithms in population-based samples, 2) whether task length is optimal, and 3) whether computational parameters help predict psychopathology (hallucinations and delusions in particular) in the general population, and how these predictors may be impacted by demographic variables, such as race, ethnicity, gender, age and other social determinants of health.

Participant demographics will be matched to the U.S. Census 2023 American Community Survey (ACS) data release (updated as available). MPI MacDonald has successfully recruited large online samples for over a decade.

Specifically, researchers will recruit two samples of n=2,000 to preregister hypotheses and then n=3,000 to independently confirm those hypotheses. Multiple methods will affirm the highest quality human self-report and behavioral data for online samples.

Researchers use Prolific, which is known for high quality research participation, maintaining low levels of bots through strategies such as requiring a photo ID and a waiting period. Second, inclusion criteria will require an approval rating of 90-100% from previous researchers. Participants will complete three sessions, each limited to \~60 min to avoid burnout.

brief_summary: This study will compare mirror therapy (MT) with motor imagery (MI), each added to routine Bobath-based physical therapy, to assess upper limb motor function and functional independence in patients with subacute middle cerebral artery (MCA) stroke. Upper limb dysfunction is a common and disabling consequence of MCA stroke, affecting reaching, grasping, manipulation and daily activities. Although MT and MI have each shown benefit, it is unclear which adjunct gives greater and longer-lasting improvement. A total of 36 adults aged 45-60 years will be randomly allocated 1:1 into an MT group or an MI group. Both groups will receive 3 supervised sessions per week for 6 weeks, followed by a 6-week home exercise program. Outcomes (Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity, Action Research Arm Test, Box and Block Test, Modified Barthel Index) will be assessed at baseline, post-intervention (Week 6) and follow-up (Week 12). The study aims to determine which intervention gives superior improvement in upper limb recovery.

The goal of this observational study is to learn about the association of inflammatory biomarkers (SII, NLR, and PLR) and ferritin with disease severity in pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus (pSLE) patients. The main question it aims to answer is:

Are higher levels of SII, NLR, PLR, and ferritin associated with greater disease severity (mild, moderate, severe based on SLEDAI-2K score) in pediatric SLE patients?

Participants diagnosed with pediatric SLE will undergo routine blood tests to measure complete blood counts (NLR, PLR, SII) and serum ferritin, and their disease severity will be assessed using the SLEDAI-2K scoring system
primary_outcomes: Pediatric SLE Disease Severity Category
title: Association of Inflammatory Biomarkers and Ferritin With Severity of Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Patients

brief_summary:
ALERT-1 is a Phase 1/2 study evaluating the safety and preliminary anti-tumor activity of SRN-101, an investigational gene therapy, in adults with recurrent high-grade glioma. High-grade glioma is a type of brain cancer. This study is for adults whose cancer has returned for the first time and for whom surgical removal of the tumor is not planned.

SRN-101 uses an adeno-associated virus (AAV) to deliver a gene for human interferon beta, a protein within the tumor. The safety and effectiveness of SRN-101 in this setting have not been established.

Each participant will receive one infusion of SRN-101 directly into the brain tumor during an MRI-guided procedure. The study will first evaluate different dose levels and then evaluate a selected dose in additional participants.

Participants will have MRI scans, blood tests and other health assessments, and follow-up visits to assess safety and changes in their cancer.
primary_outcomes: Evaluation of the safety and tolerability of SRN-101 in adult participants with recurrent high-grade glioma.
Determination of the RP2D of SRN-101
title: A Study of SRN-101 Gene Therapy in Adults With Recurrent High-Grade Glioma (ALERT-1)

brief_summary: The Department of Acupuncture-Moxibustion, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University is conducting a clinical research project entitled "Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation，taVNS) for Insomnia During the Withdrawal-Rehabilitation Period of Methamphetamine Use Disorder". This study aims to explore the short-term clinical efficacy and safety of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS), based on the theory of "Heart-Kidney Interplay", in improving insomnia among patients with methamphetamine use disorder in the withdrawal-rehabilitation period on the basis of routine drug-addiction rehabilitation. The primary efficacy outcome is the change in total score of the Insomnia Severity Index (Insomnia Severity Index,ISI) from baseline to Week 4. This project will commence in September 2026, and a total of 96 participants with methamphetamine use disorder in the withdrawal-rehabilitation period will be recruited.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University
primary_outcomes: Insomnia Severity Index
title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (taVNS) for Insomnia During the Withdrawal-Rehabilitation Period of Methamphetamine Use Disorder

brief_summary: Periodontitis is an inflammatory disease affecting the tissues that support the teeth. Scaling and root planing is a standard nonsurgical treatment, but additional local treatments may help improve clinical periodontal outcomes and reduce bacterial load. This study compared scaling and root planing alone with scaling and root planing combined with locally applied Aloe vera gel or clindamycin gel in adults with periodontitis. The study evaluated clinical periodontal parameters and anaerobic bacterial counts at baseline and at 1 and 3 months after treatment. The objective was to compare the clinical and microbiological outcomes of the three treatment approaches.
primary_outcomes: Change in Clinical Attachment Level
Change in Probing Pocket Depth
title: Comparing Aloe Vera Gel and Clindamycin Gel Added to Scaling and Root Planing for Periodontitis

brief_summary: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-standing autoimmune inflammatory disease marked by continuous synovial inflammation, which contributes to progressive cartilage and bone damage, eventually resulting in joint destruction. Both inherited genetic factors and environmental exposures substantially contribute to the risk of developing the disease. Additionally, several lifestyle and biological factors including diet, cigarette smoking, hormonal influences, alcohol consumption, gut microbiota, infections, and coffee intake have been implicated in the development and progression of RA. Clinically, RA is frequently characterized by morning stiffness, pain involving the shoulder, neck, and pelvic girdle, impaired mobility, and systemic features including fever.
primary_outcomes: Change in disease activity score (DAS-28CRP)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dapagliflozin as an Adjunct to Conventional Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary: This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to compare the effects of a computer-controlled local anesthetic delivery system (CALAJECT) and the conventional injection technique for inferior alveolar nerve block (IANB) on injection pain, heart rate, and blood pressure in adult patients. Participants requiring dental treatment of mandibular posterior teeth will be randomly assigned to receive IANB using either the CALAJECT system or the conventional injection technique. Pain experienced during the anesthetic injection will be evaluated using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Heart rate and blood pressure will be recorded before and after the injection to evaluate cardiovascular responses. The study aims to determine whether the method of local anesthetic administration influences patient-reported pain and cardiovascular responses during IANB.
interventions: Conventional Inferior Alveolar Nerve Block Injection
primary_outcomes: Pain Perception During Inferior Alveolar Nerve Block Injection

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether adults who visit a hospital emergency department (ED) find it acceptable to start HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) during that same visit, with help from a peer navigator. PrEP is a daily pill that lowers the chance of getting HIV. Many people who could benefit from PrEP use the ED for health care but have no regular doctor, so they may never be offered it.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Do participants find starting PrEP in the ED acceptable?
* How many participants take the first dose, connect with an ongoing PrEP provider, and keep taking PrEP over one year?

Patients will be randomly divided into two groups: an experimental group receiving VCT alongside standard wound care, and a control group receiving standard wound care alone. The main goal is to compare tissue oxygen levels between the treated (diseased) leg and the untreated (healthy) leg, as well as between the two patient groups before and after therapy. Researchers will also closely monitor how the wounds heal over time using standard clinical measurements and advanced digital photograph analysis (Fiji software). brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized feasibility clinical trial is to learn whether a low-cost smart sock and mobile application can be used safely, reliably, and comfortably to support gradual walking activity in adults aged 60 years and older. The smart sock is a research prototype worn with the participant's usual footwear. It records simple walking information, such as step timing and walking rhythm, and sends a summary to a mobile application. The application provides an individual walking plan, asks about perceived effort and symptoms, and shows simple messages about whether the participant should continue, repeat the current level, or pause and seek review.

The study will include community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older who can walk independently, with or without a usual walking aid when this is considered safe. This study does not diagnose medical conditions, predict falls, provide emergency monitoring, or replace medical care.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Can older adults use the smart sock and application comfortably and complete the planned walking sessions?
* Does the smart sock record step events and walking cadence accurately enough for this type of monitoring?
* Are the application instructions, safety messages, and optional family-support feature understandable and acceptable to older adults?
* Can the study procedures be delivered safely, including device fitting, battery charging, walking progression, and reporting of symptoms or falls?
* What changes are seen over 12 weeks in walking activity and supervised functional assessments?

Researchers will compare a smart-sock-supported adaptive walking group with a comparison group receiving a standard individual walking plan. Participants will be assigned to one of the two groups by chance. The smart-sock group will use the device and app, which may adjust the walking plan conservatively when repeated sessions are completed at an acceptable effort and no safety concerns are reported. Participants in this group may choose a trusted family member or helper to receive limited notifications, such as "session completed" or "please check in." Family members will not see sensor data, symptoms, health history, test results, or decisions about walking progression. The comparison group will follow a standard nonadaptive walking plan independently and will not receive the smart sock, individualized app feedback, or study-provided family support.

Participants will:

* Complete screening, provide informed consent, and take part in a supervised baseline visit.
* Complete walking-related assessments at baseline, Week 6, and Week 12, including a 6-minute walk test, Timed Up and Go test, and 30-second chair-stand test.
* Follow an individual walking plan for 12 weeks, usually with three to five sessions per week.
* In the smart-sock group, wear the smart sock during planned sessions and use the mobile application to record session completion, perceived effort, and any symptoms.
* Report falls, near-falls, pain, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, device discomfort, or technical problems.

Participants can stop a walking session at any time. The walking plan will not progress if there are warning symptoms, a fall, high perceived effort, concerning changes in walking information, or a decline at supervised reassessment. The study team may pause, simplify, or review the plan when needed.
interventions: Low-Cost Smart Sock and Older-Adult Mobile Application
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of the Low-Cost Smart Sock and Older-Adult Mobile Application Intervention

These implants are inserted into the fallopian tubes by hysteroscopy. Marketed in 2002, ESSURE® contraceptive implants were withdrawn from the French market in 2017 (and worldwide in 2017 and 2018) following the observation in certain patients of polymorphic and non-specific gynecological and extra-gynecological symptoms. The hypothesis would be a dissemination of the metallic elements contained in these implants.

Studies with small numbers and short-term follow-up have shown a significant improvement in these symptoms after implant explantation. This constitutes a real public health problem since according to the report of the Scientific Interest Group EPI-PHARE, 198,000 French women have these implants and only 30,000 of them, or 15%, have been explanted. A large number of these patients, presenting symptoms, have not yet been treated for an explant.

Although explantation of these implants is now recommended in symptomatic patients, approximately 20 to 30% of these patients remain symptomatic after explantation in the form of fibromyalgia signs. Transcutaneous electrical neurostimulation of the vagus nerve uses a non-invasive portable device that is positioned at ear level for 20 minutes per day and allows painless stimulation of the vagus nerve. This device is indicated in fibromyalgia as a non-drug and non-invasive device. This device (TENS ECO PLUS) is offered in routine practice in the service to still symptomatic patients with fibromyalgia symptoms after explantation of the Essure device. In this study, we wish to evaluate the improvement of the symptoms of these patients.
primary_outcomes: Improvement in patients' symptoms

Interventions that effectively support families in obtaining and consuming healthier food and improve dietary intake are poised to improve developmental outcomes among pediatric cancer survivors. One promising way to impact the family diet is by targeting food purchasing. Optimal defaults, or making the healthy choice the automatic choice, is a specific nudge strategy that may be a feasible, acceptable and effective way to promote healthier food purchasing and dietary intake among pediatric cancer survivors and their families.

This single-centre prospective study records ETT and TCN signals simultaneously in the same patient during thyroidectomy, so that each patient serves as their own control. The primary aim is to compare how often each electrode type shows a false amplitude decrease of more than 50% in nerves without true injury. There are currently different treatment options in the management of stress urinary incontinence (SUI). Given a risk of complications inherent to prosthetic reinforcement and numerous current controversies over the use of a synthetic material, other alternatives must be offered to patients. Peri-urethral injections of filler are increasingly becoming part of the therapeutic arsenal. This is a minimally invasive technique carried out under local anesthesia on an outpatient basis.

Peri-urethral injections are currently offered to all patients with stress urinary incontinence, due to sphincter or mixed insufficiency and particularly after suburethral sling failure.

Perineal ultrasound after injection allows you to visualize the positioning of the filler bubbles under the bladder neck. In the event of clinical ineffectiveness associated with poor position of the bubbles, this could be an argument for a 2nd injection. If, on the contrary, the bubbles are well positioned, another technique could be proposed.
