brief_summary:
Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is a common gastrointestinal disorder with a significant impact on the quality of life of patients. Its global prevalence varies considerably, estimated at up to 10%, due to differences in diagnostic criteria, cultural factors and dietary patterns. Dietary interventions have emerged as first-line strategies for symptom management, with the low Fermentable Oligo-, Di-, and Monosaccharides and Polyols (FODMAP) diet demonstrating strong efficacy in reducing gastrointestinal symptoms by minimizing poorly absorbed, fermentable carbohydrates. However, concerns about long-term nutritional adequacy, potential alterations in gut microbiota composition, and sustainability of the low-FODMAP diet have led to the need for more comprehensive and nutritionally balanced dietary models.

In contrast, the Mediterranean Diet (MD), is widely recognized for its anti-inflammatory, cardiometabolic, and potential anticancer effects. Notably, adherence to the MD has been associated with favorable gut microbial profiles and a reduced risk of colorectal and other gastrointestinal cancers. However, the high FODMAP content of many components of the MD may limit its direct compatibility with dietary protocols for IBS. Incorporating the principles of the MD into a low-FODMAP dietary approach offers a promising strategy for enhancing the nutritional quality, sustainability, and long-term effectiveness of dietary management in IBS.

The aim of the study is to investigate and compare the effectiveness of a Mediterranean Modified Low FODMAP diet (Med-Mod LFD) with standard Mediterranean dietary recommendations (Med standard) in managing the symptoms of IBS. Specifically, the study aims to evaluate the impact of the two dietary interventions on the frequency and severity of gastrointestinal symptoms, to examine potential differences in quality of life, to assess patient compliance and acceptance of the two dietary approaches, and to explore whether the Med-Mod Low FODMAP variation of the Mediterranean diet offers advantages over the classical Mediterranean diet without compromising the health-promoting characteristics that make it beneficial.Dietary intake will also be assessed using a three-day food diary, which will be used for the dietary analysis of participants' food intake and for the assessment of macro- and micronutrient intake of the two dietary interventions
primary_outcomes: Change in symptom severity from baseline to post-intervention, assessed using a validated disease-specific questionnaire.
title: Nutritional Management of the Irritable Bowel Syndrome(IBS): The Role of the Mediterranean Diet (MD)

brief_summary:
Heart failure is a condition in which the heart cannot pump blood as effectively as it should. It can cause symptoms such as shortness of breath, tiredness, and fluid retention. Vericiguat is a medication used in certain patients with heart failure whose symptoms have recently worsened.

The aim of this study is to better understand how vericiguat treatment is associated with changes in metabolism, heart function, and blood vessel health in patients with heart failure.

This is a prospective, observational study conducted at a single hospital in Italy. Researchers will collect clinical information and analyze biological samples to investigate changes in molecules involved in energy production, inflammation, and cardiovascular function. Heart imaging and assessments of blood vessel function will also be used to better understand the patients' cardiovascular health.

The study will explore whether these biological and cardiovascular measurements are associated with treatment with vericiguat and whether they could help identify patients who may benefit most from this therapy.

The results may improve our understanding of heart failure and support more personalized treatment strategies in the future.
conditions: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction
primary_outcomes: Changes in Plasma Metabolomic and Lipidomic Profiles Following Vericiguat Initiation
title: Metabolic Changes in Heart Failure Patients Treated With Vericiguat

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-blinded and randomized clinical trial, and will be conducted at Chang Gung Memorial Hospital Chiayi branch in Taiwan.

1. Why is this study being done? Inguinal hernia is a common condition in adults. It can be classified into different types, and more than half of adult inguinal hernias are belonged to the "indirect" type.

   Traditionally, inguinal hernias are repaired with artificial mesh in adults. Since 2018, we use the laparoscopy-assisted percutaneous internal ring suture (PIRS), which has been proofed to be safe and effectiveness in repairing the pediatric indirect inguinal hernia, to treat the adult indirect inguinal hernias. More than 150 adult patients were treated by using this method with good results and low recurrence rate.

   However, conventional needles for the pediatric group are too short and weak to operate on the adult group. Now there is a new device, laparoscopic non-mesh hernia needle set, designed specifically for adults. We would like to evaluate whether this new device can: (1) Shorten the operation time; (2) Reduce postoperative pain; (3) Maintain a low recurrence rate
2. What will happen to the participants

The participants, whose hernia confirmed to be the indirect type under laparoscopic inspection, would be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

(1) The control group: using conventional needle set for PIRS; (2) The experimental group: using laparoscopic non-mesh hernia needle set for PIRS.

Both groups would undergo the same surgical method except the needle devices. For the participants with inguinal hernias other than the indirect type, an adequate mesh repair be performed according to the Guideline of Hernia Surg (Hernia. 2018; 22(1): 17-18)

After surgery, three follow-up visits within six months would be arranged to all participants. Each visit will take about one hour. During these visits, we will:

(1) Record about recovery and pain conditions; (2) Check surgical wound; (3) Evaluate whether the hernia has recurred.

3\. What are the possible complications? The risks of surgery are similar whether the participants join the study or not. Possible complications include: (1) Postoperative pain; (2) Hernia recurrence; (3) Wound infection; (4) Bruising or bleeding under the skin at the needle site

This study will help us to determine whether the new needle set could decrease the complication rate.

4\. Participation in this study is completely voluntary. For the patients unwilling to participate this study, they will receive the standard procedures at present, including: (1) Open hernia repair with mesh, Lichtenstein method. (2) Laparoscopic hernia repair with mesh, TEP or TAPP. (3) Laparoscopic repair using the conventional hernia needle
conditions: Inguinal Hernia, Without Mention of Obstruction or Gangrene
primary_outcomes: post operational pain
title: Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of a New Laparoscopic Non-mesh Hernia Needle Set Designed for Indirect Inguinal Hernia

brief_summary:
This study compares two different methods of repairing fractures at the front of the lower jaw (the symphysis and parasymphysis). Usually, surgeons fix these displaced fractures using two separate titanium plates, which can be time-consuming to place and lie close to the nerve that supplies feeling to the lower lip and chin. Recently, a single Z-shaped titanium plate was designed to provide the same stability using less hardware, potentially making the surgery easier and safer for the nerve.

The purpose of this study is to compare the use of a single Z-shaped miniplate with the conventional two-miniplate technique in adult patients. The researchers will measure how long the surgery takes, the number of screws needed, and how easy it is to place the plates. After the surgery, patients will be monitored for up to 3 months to compare pain levels, facial swelling, jaw movement (mouth opening and side-to-side movement), nerve function, and how well the bone heals on x-rays.
primary_outcomes: Radiographic Evaluation of Fracture Reduction
title: Z-Shaped Versus Conventional Miniplates for Mandibular Fractures

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a self-administered digital game can improve attention, memory, and planning and reduce ADHD-like symptoms in children aged 6-12 in Hong Kong who have subclinical or vulnerable ADHD symptoms. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does playing a 30-minute digital game 5 times per week for 8 weeks improve sustained attention, memory, and planning?

Does it reduce parent- and teacher-rated inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity symptoms compared with an active control game (Tetris)?

Researchers will compare a first-wave group that receives the digital game first and then Tetris with a second-wave group that receives Tetris first and then the digital game, to see if the digital game produces greater improvements.

Participants will:

Be screened for subclinical ADHD using parent and teacher questionnaires.

Play the "Lucky Panda" digital game or Tetris for 30 minutes, 5 times a week for 8 weeks, then switch to the other activity for another 8 weeks.

Complete computer-based tasks measuring attention, memory, and planning at three time points: before the study, after the first 8 weeks, and after the second 8 weeks.

Have their parents and teachers complete ADHD symptom questionnaires at the same three time points.

Have parents report their child's interest in the game, adherence, and other digital game habits.

This study focuses on children with subclinical symptoms, not children already diagnosed with ADHD or receiving ADHD treatment. If effective, the game may offer an accessible early self-help intervention while families wait for professional care.

Memory recognition task

brief_summary:
This is a non-interventional translational research study aiming to comprehensively characterize the genomic and transcriptomic landscape of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The study will employ whole-exome sequencing (WES) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) on tumor tissue samples and matched germline DNA to identify genomic alterations, mutational signatures, and transcriptomic profiles associated with prognosis and response to immunotherapy.

A total of approximately 300 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC will be included, comprising both metastatic and early-stage disease. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue and, where available, fresh frozen samples will be analyzed. Peripheral blood samples will also be collected for germline DNA assessment. The study aims to identify clinically actionable genomic alterations, measure tumor mutational burden (TMB), characterize immune-related gene expression signatures, and investigate associations between molecular findings and clinical outcomes.

In addition, a pilot sub-study will evaluate circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics in approximately 20 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC treated with concurrent chemoradiation followed by durvalumab maintenance therapy. Longitudinal plasma samples will be collected at predefined timepoints to assess minimal residual disease (MRD), ctDNA kinetics, and correlations with clinical outcomes including progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

The results of this study are expected to improve understanding of tumor biology and immune landscape in NSCLC and support the identification of prognostic and predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy and other treatment strategies.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of genomic alterations, TMB levels, and mRNA-based immune subtypes
title: Analysis of Whole Exome and Transcriptome Sequencing to Identify Prognostic Biomarkers in Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

brief_summary: Lower extremity bone stress injury (BSI) is a common overuse injury in athletes and typically requires 4-12 weeks rehabilitation time, provided the injury does not require surgery. Current BSI treatment strategies include cessation of load-bearing sporting activities, consideration for crutches and/or immobilization, pain management, and a gradual return to activities until symptoms resolve. Premature return to sport can result in risk of complications and reinjury of the healing BSI. Moreover, our prior work reported that 1/3 of women with a tibial BSI will sustain at least one additional BSI within one year, indicating that current return to sport guidelines may be inadequate. However, there are no gold standard or validated clinical, functional or imaging outcomes that are consistently used to assess BSI healing and guide return to sport. In this prospective observational study, the investigators will enroll male and female athletes with a diagnosed BSI. The investigators will utilize diagnostic imaging, blood samples, and questionnaires to identify primary and secondary outcomes for assessing BSI healing in runners. Our long-term goal is to identify whether biomarkers, health and lifestyle factors, and training patterns associated with future BSI have the potential to inform and improve BSI treatment.

brief_summary: Eye dominance refers to the preference for one eye when processing visual information and may influence visual-motor integration and motor coordination. Although previous studies have investigated eye dominance and visual training in relation to motor control and athletic performance, evidence regarding their acute effects in volleyball players remains limited. This study aims to investigate the acute effects of eye dominance-based visual training on upper extremity motor performance in volleyball players. By evaluating a single-session, low-cost, and equipment-minimal visual training protocol, the study seeks to determine whether targeted visual exercises can produce measurable improvements in motor performance. The findings may contribute to the development of individualized visual-motor training strategies to support athletic performance and inform future research in sports science, physiotherapy, and motor control.

brief_summary:
Focal autoimmune pancreatitis (f-AIP) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibit substantial overlap in clinical manifestations and imaging features, posing a major diagnostic challenge in pancreatic diseases. Given the marked differences in treatment strategies and prognosis, accurate differentiation is essential to avoid unnecessary surgery and ensure timely initiation of anticancer treatment.

This study aims to collect endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) images from patients with confirmed f-AIP or PDAC across multiple centers, using a previously established multicenter database. Data collected before January 2026 will be used to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) model based on EUS radiomics for differential diagnosis. Subsequently, prospectively collected data from participating centers from 2026 onward will be used for model testing and validation. The diagnostic performance of the model will be evaluated and compared with that of endoscopists with different levels of experience.

Furthermore, this study will investigate the clinical value of interpretable radiomic features, with particular emphasis on challenging diagnostic scenarios, including IgG4-negative AIP, AIP with elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) levels, and PDAC with imaging features resembling those of AIP. The ultimate goal is to provide a reliable tool for accurate, noninvasive preoperative differential diagnosis while promoting the standardization of multicenter AIP databases and the sharing and utilization of imaging data resources.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) of the AI Model for Differentiating f-AIP From PDAC
title: AI-Assisted Differentiation of Autoimmune Pancreatitis and Pancreatic Cancer Using EUS: A Multicenter Ambispective Study

brief_summary:
Tuberculosis (TB) remains a global health threat with high incidence, especially in Africa. The proportion of extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) can escalate up to 36% in areas with a high HIV prevalence. Effectively managing and controlling EPTB in high-burden regions, such as Kenya, faces obstacles owing to the limitations of the current diagnostic tools. Traditional methods, such as smear microscopy and culture, often fail to detect EPTB due to the paucibacillary nature of the disease and while newer molecular techniques such as Xpert MTB/RIF have improved the diagnosis of pulmonary TB, they demonstrate reduced sensitivity for EPTB. The inadequacy of these tools results in delayed or missed diagnosis, contributing to higher morbidity and mortality. This underscores the urgent need for more sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic methods that can be applied in resource-limited settings like Kenya. This study aims to establish a biomarker-based diagnostic method for EPTB, using biomarkers such as lipoarabinomannan (LAM), MPT64, and Ag85B to diagnose and to monitor treatment response. Additionally, to clarify the characteristics and causative microorganisms of patients suspected of having TB but yielded negative results. Techniques such as ultrasensitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) and urine concentration methods will be employed to improve detection sensitivity. It also seeks to explore the extent of non-tuberculosis mycobacteria (NTM) and fungal infections in patients in patients presenting as presumed TB.

This prospective cohort study will be conducted at Kenyatta National Hospital and Mbagathi County Hospital in Nairobi, enrolling 763 adult patients with presumed extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) and 150 control participants from November 2024 to October 2028 Clinical and demographic data, along with sputum, blood, and urine samples, will be collected at enrolment for microbiological tests and biomarker analysis. The accuracy of biomarkers will be assessed by comparing their sensitivity and specificity against established diagnostic standards. For confirmed EPTB cases (n=50), follow-up samples will be collected during TB treatment to monitor biomarker trends alongside the patient's clinical progress.

This study can enhance EPTB diagnosis by evaluating the diagnostic profile of candidate biomarkers in urine or blood samples. The findings may lead to the development of accurate, non-invasive diagnostic tools suited for resource-limited settings, improving early detection and treatment outcomes. Additionally, by clarifying the epidemiological and microbiological profiles of TB, NTM, and fungal infections, the study could guide more targeted clinical management strategies, ultimately improving patient care in high-burden regions.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of candidate biomarkers
title: Biomarker Analysis for Diagnosing and Treatment Monitoring in Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis Patients in Nairobi, Kenya

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to identify the clinical, neurological, hemodynamic, and respiratory variables associated with the occurrence of adverse events during physical therapy interventions in adult neurocritical patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

What clinical, neurological, hemodynamic, and respiratory factors are associated with adverse events during physical therapy in neurocritical patients? What is the incidence and type of adverse events that occur most frequently during physical therapy in this patient population? Researchers will compare clinical and physiological data between patients who experienced adverse events during physical therapy and those who did not, to determine risk factors associated with these complications. Participants' data will be retrospectively collected from medical records without performing new clinical interventions.

brief_summary:
The BEATRICE (Benefits of cinEmA Sessions During Radio-chemoTherapy on Outcomes of Patients With ceRvIcal canCEr) study protocol aims to explore the psychological and medical benefits of cinema therapy during chemotherapy sessions for cervical cancer patients undergoing radiochemotherapy (RTCT). The study builds on prior research indicating the efficacy of art-based and immersive interventions, such as virtual reality, in reducing anxiety, distress and body symptoms in oncology patients. With a focus on personalizing cancer care, this study utilizes an immersive multimedia room where patients weekly can watch curated films during chemotherapy sessions. Endpoints include psychological outcomes, such as state anxiety, quality of life, and affective states, body perceptions, as well as medical outcomes, such as perceived treatment duration, salivary alpha-amylase levels (a stress biomarker), and clinical responses over time.

This randomized controlled trial spans 24 months, including recruitment, data collection, and analysis. Patients are assessed at three timepoints: before, immediately after, and seven days post-chemotherapy infusion, using validated psychological and quality-of-life measures. Salivary samples will also be analyzed to evaluate stress levels before and immediately after chemotherapy.

The BEATRICE study integrates technological and artistic innovation into patient care, aligning with a broader movement towards empathetic and uplifting oncology practices.

brief_summary:
This clinical study seeks to understand whether, for people with stable COPD and coronary artery calcification found on chest CT, adding traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) health guidance (including dietary guidance) based on CT calcification findings to usual care can reduce the chance of developing coronary heart disease later. The study will also examine its effects on 10-year cardiovascular disease risk, coronary artery calcification score, blood pressure, blood lipids, blood glucose, COPD acute exacerbations, lung function, quality of life, exercise tolerance, symptoms, healthcare costs, and other outcomes.

Researchers will randomly assign participants to two groups and compare:

Experimental group: usual care + TCM health guidance/dietary guidance Control group: usual care only

Group assignment will be allocated by a third-party system; neither participants nor doctors can choose the group.

Main questions:

Can TCM health guidance reduce the incidence of coronary heart disease, that is, the proportion of participants who develop new coronary heart disease after enrollment? What are its effects on 10-year cardiovascular disease risk, coronary artery calcification score, blood pressure, blood lipids, blood glucose, COPD acute exacerbations, lung function, quality of life, exercise tolerance, symptoms, and health economic indicators? What adverse reactions or discomfort will participants experience?

Participants will:

First complete questionnaires and undergo tests such as lung function and chest CT to determine whether they are eligible; After meeting the criteria and signing the consent form, be randomly assigned to the experimental group or the control group; In the experimental group, receive TCM health guidance/dietary guidance in addition to usual care; the control group will continue usual care only; Undergo routine blood and urine tests, liver and kidney function tests, blood tests, electrocardiogram, chest imaging, lung function tests, and other examinations before the intervention and at 12 months; Have cardiovascular disease risk, COPD acute exacerbations, quality of life, symptoms, blood pressure, blood glucose, blood lipids, exercise tolerance, etc. recorded before the intervention and at 6 and 12 months; Be followed for about 2 years and visit the hospital on time. Who can participate: People aged 20-80 years with a confirmed diagnosis of stable COPD, coronary artery calcification on chest CT (Agatston score \> 0), who volunteer to participate and can cooperate with follow-up. People who have existing coronary heart disease, are pregnant or breastfeeding, have severe heart, liver, or kidney disease, active pulmonary tuberculosis, or pulmonary embolism, or have received tumor treatment within the past 5 years, etc., cannot participate.

Costs: The study will pay for study-related examinations such as lung function, routine blood and urine tests, electrocardiogram, liver and kidney function, and chest imaging, and will provide TCM health guidance free of charge. Treatment and tests for other coexisting diseases, and the costs of switching to other treatments because the study treatment is ineffective, are not covered.

Possible benefits: You may experience improvement in your condition and receive good medical care; the results of this study may help doctors find better ways to manage cardiovascular risk in people with COPD. Possible risks: There may be discomfort, changes in your condition, ineffective treatment, inconvenience from traveling to the hospital, or privacy breaches. If you experience any discomfort, tell your doctor promptly. This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan University of Chinese Medicine.

brief_summary:
Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM) using motor evoked potentials (MEP) and somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) is routinely applied during spinal tumor resection to detect impending neurological injury. Propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia suppresses MEP amplitude in a dose-dependent manner, which can generate false-positive alerts and complicate interpretation of IONM signals. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine whose effect on evoked potentials during spine surgery has not been well characterized.

This prospective, single-center, randomized, parallel-group, superiority trial compares remimazolam-based versus propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia in adults undergoing elective spinal tumor resection with combined MEP and SEP monitoring. The primary hypothesis is that remimazolam better preserves MEP amplitude than propofol during the critical period of tumor manipulation.

A total of 190 participants will be randomized 1:1. The primary outcome is the mean MEP amplitude of target muscles recorded during the critical period of tumor manipulation, expressed as a percentage of the pre-incision baseline value. The key secondary outcome is the incidence of intraoperative IONM alert events. Participants are followed for 30 days after surgery.
primary_outcomes: MEP amplitude preservation ratio during the critical period of tumor manipulation
title: Remimazolam vs Propofol for Motor and Somatosensory Evoked Potentials in Spinal Tumor Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will compare perturbation-based balance training (PBBT) with conventional balance training in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy to assess reactive stepping ability, dynamic balance, and functional balance. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes, affecting nearly 43% of diabetic patients in Pakistan. As a progressive condition, it leads to peripheral sensory loss, proprioceptive deficits, and delayed neuromuscular responses, all of which compromise balance and postural control and place this population at significantly elevated risk of falls.

In this study, a total of 40 adults with DPN will be randomly allocated into two groups: PBBT and CBT. Both groups will receive a total of 24 sessions with 3 supervised sessions per week for 8 weeks. The PBBT group will receive manually delivered, repeated, unexpected perturbations by a physical therapist. The CBT group will receive conventional balance training without perturbations. Outcome measures will include reactive stepping (Lean-and-Release Test), dynamic balance (Mini-BESTest), and functional balance (Berg Balance Scale). The assessment will be done at baseline, post-intervention (Week 8), and follow-up (Week 12). The study aims to determine which intervention provides superior improvement in reactive stepping and balance in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

primary_outcomes: Reactive stepping ability (Lean-and-Release Test)
title: Effects of Perturbation-Based Versus Conventional Balance Training on Reactive Stepping Ability in Patients With Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether adding a short educational animation to standard preoperative information can help reduce anxiety in adolescents aged 12-17 years who are scheduled for elective surgery.

A total of 148 adolescents will participate in this randomized controlled study. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The first group will receive standard verbal and written information about anesthesia. The second group will receive the same information along with an age-appropriate educational animation explaining what to expect before, during, and after anesthesia.

Participants will be asked to rate their anxiety before receiving information in the preoperative waiting area and again in the operating room before receiving any sedative medication or anesthesia. The researchers will compare how anxiety levels change between the two groups.

The study will also assess heart rate, blood pressure, parental anxiety, satisfaction with the information provided, and adolescents' feelings about their upcoming surgery.

The findings may help healthcare professionals improve the way adolescents and their families are prepared for anesthesia and surgery.

They will take the study product starting 7 days before radiation therapy and continue until 6 weeks after the radiation therapy ends.

Researchers will closely monitor and compare the occurrence of diarrhea and other side effects between the two groups to see if the KAWAI supplement is safe and effective in improving patients' quality of life during radiotherapy. A total of 100 participants are expected to be enrolled.

brief_summary:
Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of pain, disability, and reduced physical functioning worldwide. Although physiotherapy and physical activity are recommended as first-line treatments, many individuals with knee OA do not achieve or maintain recommended levels of physical activity. As a result, the benefits of evidence-based physiotherapy are often not fully realized. To improve physical activity participation, effective behaviour change interventions are needed.

Theory-informed interventions have the potential to enhance physiotherapy outcomes by targeting the psychological determinants that influence physical activity behaviour. One well-established framework is the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), which proposes that behaviour is primarily influenced by behavioural intention, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control. To translate these determinants into intervention content, behaviour change techniques (BCTs) can be systematically selected using tools such as the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology (BCIO), Mechanisms of Action Ontology (MoAO), and Theory and Techniques Tool (TaTT). This approach may improve the effectiveness and sustainability of behaviour change interventions.

The present study therefore aims to evaluate the potential of a TPB-based behaviour change intervention as an addition to guideline-recommended physiotherapy for individuals with knee OA. The primary objective is to determine whether this theory-driven intervention can improve physical activity levels and reduce sedentary behaviour. A secondary objective is to explore the behavioural mechanisms through which these changes occur.

The study will employ a randomized, concurrent, multiple-baseline single-case experimental design (SCED). Participants with knee OA will receive a six-week physiotherapy intervention consisting of usual guideline-based care supplemented with a TPB-based behaviour change component. Physical activity and sedentary behaviour will be continuously assessed using ActiGraph accelerometers. In addition, behavioural determinants, pain, and functional limitations will be repeatedly measured to evaluate potential mechanisms of action and clinical effects. Findings from this study may contribute to the development of more effective, theory-informed physiotherapy interventions aimed at promoting sustainable physical activity behaviour in people with knee OA.
primary_outcomes: Change in physical activity (ActiGraph GT3x) from Phase A to Phase B to Phase A'.
Change in sedentary behaviour (ActiGraph GT3x) from Phase A to Phase B to Phase A'.
title: The Effect of Theory-driven Physiotherapy on Physical Activity in Knee OA.

brief_summary:
This study tests whether a five-day Empathy and Communication Training Program (ECTP) helps psychiatric nurse specialists in Saudi Arabia engage better with their patients. Good relationships between nurses and patients are central to mental health care, but structured training in empathy and communication is limited in Saudi psychiatric hospitals.

The ECTP is a face-to-face program of five two-hour sessions (10 hours in total). It covers empathy and communication, the work environment, language and cultural barriers, and emotional preparedness. Sessions use short lectures, role-play, case discussions and group reflection.

The study took place at two psychiatric hospitals. Nurses at the Eradah Complex for Mental Health in Dammam took the ECTP. Nurses at the Eradah Hospital for Mental Health in Madinah attended their usual hospital training sessions instead. Participants were not randomly assigned. The hospital they worked in decided which group they joined.

Nurses at both hospitals completed a 15-item questionnaire about therapeutic engagement before and after the training period. After the program, 15 nurses from the Dammam group were interviewed about how the training affected their work and what barriers remained.

The study aims to find out whether nurses' self-reported therapeutic engagement improves after the ECTP compared with usual training, and to understand nurses' own experiences of the program.
primary_outcomes: Change in overall nurse-reported patient therapeutic engagement (PTE) score
title: Empathy and Communication Training Program for Psychiatric Nurse Specialists in Saudi Arabia (ECTP)

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the effects of contralateral gravity-eliminated gluteus medius strengthening and ipsilateral quadratus lumborum strengthening, both combined with conventional physiotherapy, on pelvic alignment, balance, and functional mobility in patients with subacute stroke. This single-blinded, two-arm, parallel-group randomized clinical trial will be conducted at the Department of Physical Therapy Rehabilitation, Alfalah Medical Center, Lahore, Pakistan. A total of 40 participants aged 45-60 years with a first-ever stroke occurring 1-6 months before enrollment will be recruited and randomly allocated to two groups. Group A will receive 30 minutes of conventional physiotherapy followed by 20 minutes of contralateral gravity-eliminated gluteus medius strengthening, while Group B will receive 30 minutes of conventional physiotherapy followed by 20 minutes of ipsilateral quadratus lumborum strengthening. Both groups will receive treatment three times per week for six weeks. The primary outcome measures will include pelvic alignment assessed using the Palpation Meter (PALM), balance assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and functional mobility assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test. All outcome measures will be assessed at baseline, immediately after the six-week intervention, and at week 12 to evaluate changes following treatment and at follow-up. The study will compare outcomes between the two groups to determine the relative effectiveness of the two targeted strengthening approaches when combined with conventional physiotherapy in patients with subacute stroke.

brief_summary:
FOS-PROST was a prospective, non-randomized, controlled phase IV clinical trial designed to evaluate the clinical and microbiological efficacy of oral fosfomycin trometamol as sequential antibiotic therapy in patients with acute bacterial prostatitis caused by multidrug-resistant \*Escherichia coli\*.

According to the study protocol, patients with multidrug-resistant \*E. coli\* were assigned to receive oral fosfomycin trometamol, whereas patients with non-multidrug-resistant \*E. coli\* were assigned to receive conventional oral antibiotic treatment with ciprofloxacin or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, according to antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

All patients received 1 to 5 days of appropriate intravenous antibiotic therapy before switching to oral treatment. Fosfomycin trometamol was administered at a standard dose of 3 g once daily. The planned total duration of antibiotic treatment was 21 days in both groups, including intravenous and oral therapy.

During study conduct, some patients with non-multidrug-resistant \*E. coli\* also received fosfomycin. All patients with multidrug-resistant \*E. coli\* received fosfomycin.

Clinical and microbiological outcomes were compared between treatment groups. Secondary objectives included evaluating carbapenem consumption, hospital length of stay, safety, recurrence, and fosfomycin pharmacokinetics.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Clinical Cure
Percentage of Participants With Microbiological Cure

brief_summary:
Cigarette smoking remains the leading modifiable risk factor for lung cancer4 and 16 other types of cancer, as well as chronic cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases. Despite public health efforts, smoking prevalence remains a major national as well as international challenge. Currently in Norway 16% of those 25-74 years of age are still daily or occasional smokers (9% and 7%, respectively), projecting a 10% of smoking prevalence during the current decade. In Europe it was estimated to be more than 183 millions current and former smokers (42% of the population) in 2017. Thus, smoking is a central public health issue nationally and internationally.

Smoking cessation not only significantly reduces lung cancer risk and other smoking related diseases, but also improves life expectancy, making this intervention a critical component of primary cancer prevention. Despite a decline in smoking rates, approximately 10% of Norwegians still smoke, with non-daily smoking on the rise among young people (16-24 years), affecting 19% of men and 13% of women. This underscores the urgent need for more effective cessation strategies.

A number of smoking cessation treatments have been developed, but the majority of people relapse within the first year of cessation. Primary care faces significant barriers in delivering effective smoking cessation interventions.

On the clinician side, challenges include a lack of personalized treatment options, time constraints, and unclear guidelines. From the patient perspective, there is often a lack of motivation and a perception that treatments are not tailored to individual needs.

This project aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a newly developed, personalized smoking cessation app designed to assists GPs in providing tailored smoking cessation treatments. Specifically, we will test whether the use of this app results in improved smoking cessation outcomes and enhanced quality of life for smokers in primary healthcare settings, compared to the current standard smoking cessation treatments.

Based on the results from the app, GPs will receive advice on how to motivate this particular person to quit smoking. The point of the app is that healthcare professionals will be able to provide a more personalized smoking cessation treatment based on the information that the smoker has entered into the app compared to current practice. Our hypothesis is that by using our newly developed app, healthcare professionals will be able to achieve better smoking cessation results compared to the standard smoking cessation approach used today.

The project is a clinical randomized-controlled phase 3 study in which we, through GP offices across the country, will include smokers who want to quit smoking to test this app. The intervention group (n=310) will be a group of smokers where the GP uses the app to help them quit smoking, while the control group (n=310) will be smokers who only receive regular smoking cessation treatment as is currently provided by GPs.

The health benefits of increased smoking cessation success rates are major, including prevention of various cancers as well as other chronic smoking-related diseases such as cardiovascular disease and lung disease e.g. COPD. This will in turn provide significant cost savings at a societal level.
primary_outcomes: Rate of smoking cessation
title: New Smoking Cessation Intervention in Primary Care - a Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is the leading cause of sepsis-related death. Early in sepsis, intestinal barrier injury and gut microbiota dysbiosis occur, and gut-derived toxins and inflammatory cytokines act on the lungs and the whole body via the gut-liver-lung axis, representing an important pathophysiological mechanism. In the intermediate and late stages of the disease, patients generally develop immunosuppression. Our team intends to establish a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)-based comprehensive intestinal management protocol. Xuanbai Chengqi Decoction will be used in early sepsis. In the intermediate-to-late stage, when immunosuppression occurs (monocytic HLA-DR \[mHLA-DR\] expression \<30%, decreased CD3+ and CD4+ lymphocyte counts, and a reduced CD4+/CD8+ ratio), Xuanbai Yiqi Decoction supplemented with forest-cultivated ginseng will be used, combined with acupuncture, to protect multiple organs including the intestine and lungs and to modulate immunity.This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial enrolling 280 patients with sepsis hospitalized in the Department of Emergency Medicine and the Department of Critical Care Medicine at Ruijin Hospital. Patients with sepsis who meet all inclusion and exclusion criteria at admission will be randomly assigned to the control group, Xuanbai Chengqi Decoction group, Xuanbai Chengqi Decoction plus forest-cultivated ginseng group, or Xuanbai Yiqi Decoction group. The granules will be dissolved in 100 mL of warm water and administered once daily via a nasogastric tube for 7 consecutive days, in addition to standard sepsis treatment.The primary outcome is improvement in the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score at day 7 (a measure of organ function). Secondary outcomes include disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) score, coagulation tests, endothelial injury and platelet markers, inflammatory markers, 28-day mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay, and adverse events.The study is funded by Ruijin Hospital and is conducted as an investigator-initiated trial.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change in SOFA score from baseline to Day 7
title: Xuanbai Yiqi Decoction for Sepsis: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:

Participants who undergo usual asessment for milk allergy (that is IgE measurement in blood and oral food provocation) will be asked to

brief_summary:

The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* Does whole-body vibration training improve dynamic postural stability in young soccer players?
* Does combining whole-body vibration with progressive balance exercises provide greater improvements in dynamic postural stability than whole-body vibration alone?

Researchers compared three groups: a control group (CON), a whole-body vibration group (WBV), and a whole-body vibration combined with balance exercises group (WBV+BE).

Participants:

* Were randomly assigned to one of the three groups.
* Completed an eight-week intervention period, with supervised training sessions three times per week in the intervention groups.
* Performed progressive balance exercises during vibration exposure in the WBV+BE group.
* Underwent dynamic postural stability assessments before and after the intervention using the Biodex Balance System.

brief_summary: Sugar substitutes are increasingly used to reduce sugar intake. SÜVY is a food ingredient combining erythritol and polydextrose. brief_summary: This clinical trial studies how different ways of using oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) affect nicotine delivery, appeal, and side effects among adult cigarette smokers. ONPs are tobacco-free nicotine products that contain nicotine but no tobacco leaf and are used by placing them between the lip and gum. Because ONPs are not burned and do not contain tobacco leaf, they are being studied as a replacement for tobacco products to lower harmful effects, particularly among adult cigarette smokers. However, previous research on ONP use has often been done via controlled assessments which had users place them in one area of the mouth, which does not reflect how they are used in the real-world. Researchers believe this approach leaves gaps in knowledge on how nicotine is delivered, sensory effects, craving and withdrawal, appeal, and side effects. This trial will have participants use ONPs in different ways, such as placed between the upper lip and gum, placed between the lower lip and gum, and placing them however they would like. brief_summary:
This study asks whether the current weight-gain guideline for pregnant people with obesity should be lowered, and whether the answer depends on how severe the obesity is. The guideline from the Institute of Medicine (IOM) recommends that all pregnant people with obesity gain 5.0 to 9.0 kg, regardless of obesity class. However, growing evidence suggests that people with Class II or III obesity may benefit from gaining less than this range-or even losing a small amount of weight-without harming the baby. A randomized trial to test this directly would be ethically and practically difficult, so this study uses a different approach: it reconstructs what such a trial would have shown, using nationwide U.S. birth records.

The study uses 2024 U.S. birth certificate data for people with pre-pregnancy obesity who had a single live birth. It compares three weight-gain patterns during pregnancy: (1) net weight loss (less than 0 kg gained), (2) restrictive gain (weight gained, but below the dynamic, gestational-age-specific IOM lower bound), and (3) standard gain within the IOM-recommended range. The main questions are whether restrictive gain or weight loss, compared with standard gain, reduces the risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (such as gestational hypertension and preeclampsia) while not increasing the risk of a baby born small for gestational age (SGA). The study also examines whether the balance of benefits and harms differs across Class I, Class II, and Class III obesity.

This is an observational study, not a randomized trial. It does not enroll participants or provide treatment. All analyses use existing, de-identified public health data. Results are intended to inform whether future weight-gain guidelines should provide class-specific recommendations rather than a single range for all obesity classes.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai First Maternal and Infant Health Hospital affiliated to Tongji University Medical School
primary_outcomes: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy (HDP)
Small for Gestational Age (SGA)
title: Gestational Weight Loss and Restrictive Weight Gain in Maternal Obesity: A Target Trial Emulation

brief_summary:
Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory disease that affects 125 million people around the world with major repercussions on physical and emotional quality of life of patients.

Many studies confirmed the association between psoriasis and comorbidities as cardio vascular diseases, gastroinstestinal, kidney diseases, cancers, infections or mood disorders. Psoriasis, specially, when it is severe, is associated with highest mortality and a disease burden linked to comorbidities. Understanding this disease burden associated to psoriasis is crucial for an optimal medical care.

Tildrakizumab is indicated in treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who need a systemic treatment, also, in case of failure, intolerance or contraindication to a systemic treatment, including Methotrexate.

The aim of TILFLEX study is to evaluate the efficacy, safety and flexibility of Tildrakizumab in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis with disease burden and/or body weight \> 90Kg.

The main objective is to evaluate the efficacy of Tildrakizumab 200mg at week (W)28.

brief_summary:
Primary hypothyroidism is a common condition, affecting nearly 10% of the general population. Its treatment is levothyroxine, a synthetic thyroid hormone with a half-life of nearly eight days. Optimal absorption of levothyroxine occurs when it is taken on an empty stomach. It is generally recommended to take the medication in the morning, at least 30 minutes before breakfast. However, this treatment regimen can be challenging for some patients. Missed doses constitute a problem, leading some patients to choose another timing of intake. Other patients may find it difficult to wait before breakfast, resulting in suboptimal absorption, increased TSH levels, and poor disease control.

Despite these challenges, American Thyroid Association guidelines recommend taking levothyroxine in the morning, in a fasting state, as the preferred timing of intake. They also suggest bedtime intake as a reasonable alternative, as long as the medication is taken at least three hours after the evening meal. As optimal levothyroxine absorption depends primarily on intake on an empty stomach, alternative treatment schedules could be considered, as long as the fasting requirement is respected to maintain stable TSH levels.

To our knowledge, only one study has compared daytime levothyroxine intake, three hours after breakfast, with morning and bedtime intake. There was no significant difference in TSH levels between the different schedules. Confirming the stability of TSH levels with different schedules would offer patients with hypothyroidism greater flexibility in treatment timing, better adapted to their lifestyle habits.

The aim of our study is to compare serum TSH levels according to two timings of levothyroxine intake in patients with hypothyroidism. Secondary objectives are to assess treatment adherence, quality of life, and patients' preferred timing of levothyroxine intake.
primary_outcomes: Stability of TSH levels with both timing of intake
title: Comparison of Two Timings of Levothyroxine Intake in Hypothyroid Patients: A Cross-over Randomized Control Trial

brief_summary:
Dissatisfaction with penile size and aesthetics may negatively affect men's self-esteem and quality of life, representing a relevant factor in psychological and sexual health. Intimate aesthetic procedures have increasingly been sought as an alternative to improve body perception and male confidence. Among the available techniques, the use of botulinum toxin and hyaluronic acid-based fillers has demonstrated potential to increase penile circumference and reduce the retraction reflex, providing functional and aesthetic benefits. However, the literature lacks robust studies evaluating the efficacy, safety, and psychological impact of these interventions.

The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and level of satisfaction associated with male intimate harmonization methods using botulinum toxin and hyaluronic acid. In addition, the study aims to analyze the effects of these techniques on patients' self-esteem and body perception, particularly in individuals with small penis syndrome or anxiety related to penile size.

This is a prospective clinical trial. Participants will be selected according to predefined criteria and will undergo an initial evaluation by a urologist. On the first day, Dysport 300SU botulinum toxin will be administered along the length of the penis, with 60% of the volume concentrated near the base. Patients will use a penile extender for at least four hours per day until the follow-up visit, scheduled 15 days after administration. At this visit, measurements of penile length and circumference will be obtained in both flaccid and erect states, followed by the administration of hyaluronic acid for penile filling. The final evaluation will take place after 30 days for a new measurement of the parameters.

The procedures are expected to result in a significant increase in penile size and circumference, as well as improvements in body perception, self-esteem, and sexual satisfaction among participants. Furthermore, this study intends to contribute to the scientific evidence base regarding male intimate aesthetics by providing evidence on the safety and efficacy of the proposed techniques and assisting in the standardization of these interventions in clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Change in penile circumference
title: Male Intimate Harmonization: Efficacy, Satisfaction, and Safety

brief_summary:
Approximately 25 participants aged 18-70 years, with knee pain rated 4-7 on a 10-point visual analogue scale (VAS) and a disease duration of 6 months to 10 years, will be enrolled. The study has two parts. In Part 1, participants receive a single intra-articular injection of 1.0 mL, 1.5 mL or 2.0 mL of study product (3-5 participants per dose level, given in ascending order). In Part 2, the dose with the most favourable balance of efficacy and safety in Part 1 is given weekly by intra-articular injection for 2-3 doses to an additional 6-10 participants.

Participants are followed for 12 weeks after the last injection. Safety is assessed through adverse events (graded by CTCAE v5.0), vital signs, physical examination, electrocardiogram, clinical laboratory tests (haematology, urinalysis, liver and kidney biochemistry, coagulation) and pregnancy testing. Efficacy is assessed by change from baseline in knee X-ray, knee MRI, the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), the WOMAC index, pain VAS and pain-free walking distance at 4 and 12 weeks after the last dose.

The study has no placebo or active comparator group. There is no plan to market the product on the basis of this study.

The intervention group will participate in the program twice a week for 11 weeks, with each session lasting 45 minutes. The program combines football-based physical activities with health education. The control group will not receive the program.

Students in both groups will undergo physical fitness and health assessments before and after the intervention. These assessments will include jumping performance, balance, change-of-direction performance, flexibility, body fat percentage, blood pressure, and resting heart rate. Researchers will compare changes in these measures between the two groups to evaluate the effects of the program.

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective, non-interventional study is to evaluate the predictive performance and potential clinical utility of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based virtual follow-up framework for incidentally detected pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs), including pure ground-glass and part-solid nodules.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Can the AI model accurately predict future CT appearances, quantitative growth characteristics, and morphological progression of pulmonary SSNs at specified follow-up intervals?
2. Does AI-assisted virtual follow-up improve radiologists' assessment of nodule progression and simulated surveillance management decisions compared with assessment without AI assistance?

Researchers will compare radiologists' assessments with and without access to AI-generated future CT images and quantitative predictions. An additional reader evaluation will examine whether generated future images provide incremental value beyond quantitative predictions alone.

Participants will undergo clinically indicated CT examinations and receive routine care according to standard clinical practice. The research team will:

* Collect previously acquired CT images and clinical information.
* Generate and lock AI predictions before the corresponding follow-up CT examinations occur.
* Obtain and lock radiologists' assessments and simulated management recommendations before actual follow-up outcomes become available.
* Compare predicted nodule progression with observed follow-up CT findings.

AI predictions and research-related reader assessments will not be disclosed to treating clinicians or used to alter patients' actual surveillance or treatment decisions.

primary_outcomes: Change in radiologists' future nodule growth discrimination (AUC)

brief_summary:
Heart failure (HF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome characterized by substantial inter-individual variability in pathophysiology and response to treatment. Precision medicine approaches are therefore needed to better account for this heterogeneity and tailor therapeutic strategies to individual patients. Virtual human twins represent one such approach, integrating multimodal clinical, biological, imaging, physiological, and omics data into patient-specific computational models to model disease mechanisms and predict individual therapeutic response.

VITAL-HF is a prospective cohort pilot study designed to clinically evaluate the ability of the VITAL cardiovascular virtual human twin to predict individual response to spironolactone in patients with HF. Adult patients with HF with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \> 40% who have a clinical indication for spironolactone as part of routine care will be enrolled and followed for 3 months. The primary objective is to assess the ability of the VITAL cardiovascular virtual human twin to discriminate responders from non-responders to spironolactone. Response is defined as a ≥20% reduction in NT-proBNP levels 3 months after spironolactone initiation.

Virtual twin predictions will be generated for research purposes only and will not influence treatment decisions or patient management.
interventions: Data collection for the development and validation of the cardiovascular virtual human twin
primary_outcomes: Discriminative performance of the VITAL cardiovascular virtual human twin for predicting response to spironolactone

brief_summary:
Early detection of atrial fibrillation detected after stroke (AFDAS) is crucial for secondary stroke prevention, as initiating direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) can reduce atrial fibrillation (AF)-related stroke risk by up to 60%. In cryptogenic stroke (CS), AFDAS likely represents the most frequent underlying etiology, yet paroxysmal and short-duration AF episodes often elude standard monitoring. The Graz AF Risk Score, implemented across all Neurology Departments in Styria, Austria, stratifies patients into tailored monitoring pathways but remains limited by delays in implantable loop recorder (ILR) implantation, patient refusal, and restricted access to early ambulatory ECG monitoring.

The study aims to close diagnostic gaps in the current AF detection pathway by implementing a non-invasive, wrist-worn photoplethysmography (PPG) device (i.e., CardioWatch 287-2 \[CW2\]) for early cardiac rhythm monitoring in CS patients.

Methods:

CATCH-AF is an investigator-initiated, prospective, longitudinal, multi-center, pre-post interventional study including all CS patients admitted to one of five Styrian Neurology Departments. In the pre-intervention phase, AF detection will follow the established Graz AF Risk Score-based algorithm. In the intervention phase, CardioWatch 287-2 screening will replace Holter-ECG screening in moderate-risk patients and will be used for high-risk patients with delayed or declined ILR implantation. Suspected AF episodes will be confirmed by ECG- based assessment at the discretion of the treating cardiologist. The primary endpoint isAFDAS detection at 3 months; secondary endpoints include AFDAS at 12 months, time to AF detection and DOAC initiation, cerebrovascular event recurrence, cardiovascular death, and all-cause mortality at 3 and 12 months. Data will be collected via REDCap and analyzed using descriptive, univariable, and multivariable regression methods, adjusted for confounders with inverse probability of treatment weighting.

The investigators hypothesize that CardioWatch 287-2 implementation will increase early AFDAS detection and reduce diagnostic and therapeutic delays, potentially lowering recurrent cerebrovascular events and mortality over 12 months.

CATCH-AF represents the first European, population-wide evaluation of a wrist-worn PPG device integrated into an established AF detection pathway for cryptogenic stroke, aiming to improve early diagnosis, treatment initiation and secondary prevention outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of atrial fibrillation detected after stroke (AFDAS) within 3 months post-stroke
title: CATCH AF - Atrial Fibrillation Detection in Cryptogenic Stroke

brief_summary:
This study is a prospective, multicenter, observational clinical study designed to collect multimodal ultrasound data to support the research and development of intelligent ultrasound imaging and autonomous ultrasound scanning robotic technologies.

The study will be conducted at three hospitals in China: Hangzhou First People's Hospital, Hangzhou Cancer Hospital, and Tonglu County First People's Hospital.

Adults aged 18 to 80 years who are scheduled to undergo routine clinical ultrasound examinations may be invited to participate. The examinations may include the hepatobiliary system, pancreas, spleen, thyroid, carotid arteries, kidneys, urinary bladder, and prostate.

Participants will undergo their usual ultrasound examinations without changes to their clinical diagnosis or treatment. A lightweight position and orientation sensor will be attached to the non-patient-contact side of the existing ultrasound probe to record probe movements while ultrasound images and videos are collected. The study will also collect information about standard imaging planes, lesions, measurements, image quality, and routine breathing or positioning instructions given by the examining clinician.

Verbal instructions will be processed locally within the hospital's controlled data environment. Only confirmed structured information about predefined instructions and their timestamps will be retained for research purposes. Raw audio recordings will not be transferred outside the hospital.

The study aims to collect 100,000 valid ultrasound data units, including 51,000 units in the first phase. A participant may contribute more than one data unit. The collected data will undergo quality control, de-identification or anonymization, and institutional data security review before any approved external use.

This study does not involve experimental medications, invasive procedures, or robotic scanning performed on participants. Participation is not expected to provide direct medical benefits. The study may help improve data collection methods and support future development of intelligent ultrasound and autonomous scanning technologies. Research data will be handled in accordance with the approved study protocol, informed consent, and applicable data protection requirements.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Number of Valid Multimodal Ultrasound Data Units
title: A Clinical Multimodal Data Collection Study for the Development of Autonomous Ultrasound Scanning Robotic Technology

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbot developed to address breastfeeding problems on mothers' breastfeeding attitudes, behaviors, and self-efficacy. The study will also assess exclusive breastfeeding rates, breastfeeding duration, and the technical performance and usability of the developed chatbot.

The study is planned to include 92 primiparous mothers allocated to intervention and control groups. The intervention involves an AI-based breastfeeding counseling chatbot developed using natural language processing (NLP) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology. The chatbot will provide evidence-based breastfeeding education, information, and counseling support using an expert-reviewed breastfeeding knowledge base. The system is designed to support mothers in managing breastfeeding-related difficulties and will not provide medical diagnoses or replace healthcare professionals.

Breastfeeding attitudes, self-efficacy, and behaviors will be evaluated during the postpartum follow-up period. Assessments will be conducted at baseline and at the first, third, and sixth postpartum months. Exclusive breastfeeding rates and breastfeeding duration will also be assessed.

Additionally, the chatbot's technical performance, response reliability, medical safety, user satisfaction, and usability will be evaluated. The study aims to provide scientific evidence regarding the effectiveness and feasibility of an AI-supported, evidence-based breastfeeding counseling intervention.
primary_outcomes: Exclusive Breastfeeding at Six Months Postpartum
title: Effect of a Breastfeeding Chatbot on Mothers' Breastfeeding Attitudes, Behaviors, and Self-Efficacy

brief_summary:
Apathy is one of the most common and undertreated neurobehavioral symptoms in older adults with dementia. It is associated with reduced motivation and engagement in daily activities, and may contribute to faster cognitive and functional decline. Currently, there are no approved pharmacologic treatments for apathy, and many behavioral interventions are difficult for individuals with apathy to initiate and sustain.

This ISAC-funded pilot study will examine the feasibility of a home-delivered, network-based transcranial direct current stimulation intervention designed to target and non-invasively stimulate brain regions involved in motivation and goal-directed behavior, including the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex. The study will assess feasibility, safety, adherence of this intervention for older adults with dementia and apathy, and obtain preliminary data of clinical and neurophysiological measures. The team has submitted the IRB application, which is currently pending review, and has posted a position to hire a new research assistant who will support recruitment, study coordination, and intervention delivery. These start-up activities will help prepare the team to launch participant enrollment once regulatory approvals and staffing are in place.
primary_outcomes: Participant Retention Rate
title: Network-based tDCS for Apathy
